1173	// doJSON performs an HTTP request with a JSON request body, decoding the JSON
1174	// response into out. Mirrors do's error handling. The 404→ErrNotFound branch is
1175	// inert for the batch POST callers (AuthorAccounts/AccountIdentities): their
1176	// contract is "absent keys omitted, not 404" — a 404 from those paths means a
1177	// misrouted request, and callers treat it as a generic resolve failure (degrade).
1178	func (c *Client) doJSON(ctx context.Context, method, url string, body, out any) error {
1179		return c.doJSONHeaders(ctx, method, url, body, out, nil)
1180	}
1181	
1182	func (c *Client) doJSONHeaders(ctx context.Context, method, url string, body, out any, headers map[string]string) error {
1183		buf, err := json.Marshal(body)
1184		if err != nil {
1185			return fmt.Errorf("coreapi: marshal request: %w", err)
1186		}
1187		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, method, url, bytes.NewReader(buf))
1188		if err != nil {
1189			return fmt.Errorf("coreapi: new request: %w", err)
1190		}
1191		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
1192		req.Header.Set("Accept", "application/json")
1193		for key, value := range headers {
1194			req.Header.Set(key, value)
1195		}
1196		resp, err := c.httpClient.Do(req)
1197		if err != nil {
1198			return fmt.Errorf("coreapi: %s %s: %w", method, url, err)
1199		}
1200		defer func() { _ = resp.Body.Close() }()
1201		if resp.StatusCode == http.StatusNotFound {
1202			return ErrNotFound
1203		}
1204		if resp.StatusCode >= 400 {
1205			preview, _ := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 4096))
1206			return &StatusError{Method: method, URL: url, Status: resp.StatusCode, Body: strings.TrimSpace(string(preview))}
1207		}
1208		if out == nil {
1209			return nil
1210		}
1211		if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(out); err != nil {
1212			return fmt.Errorf("coreapi: decode response: %w", err)
1213		}
1214		return nil
1215	}
1216	
1217	// maxPlausibleExpiresIn bounds a reported expires_in before it is converted.
1218	// GitHub App installation tokens last ~1h, so anything beyond a day is a
1219	// producer bug rather than a long-lived credential — and converting it is
1220	// unsafe regardless: a float->int64 conversion whose value is out of range is
1221	// IMPLEMENTATION-DEPENDENT in Go, saturating to MaxInt64 on arm64 but returning
1222	// MinInt64 on amd64. Unguarded, one absurd number silently yields an expiry in
1223	// either 2318 or 1734 depending on the build host.
1224	const maxPlausibleExpiresIn = 24 * time.Hour
1225	
1226	// expiresInToExpiry turns an expires_in into an absolute expiry, reporting the
1227	// zero Time for anything it cannot use.
1228	//
1229	// It never fails the caller. expires_in is not required for the access_token to
1230	// be usable, so a shape this cannot parse must cost the expiry and nothing else.
1231	// Decoding it strictly alongside access_token would instead fail the whole mint
1232	// on a value previously ignored outright, turning a cosmetic wire difference
1233	// into a dead credential and a blocking gate.
1234	//
1235	// A negative expires_in is honoured as a past instant, so a caller's freshness
1236	// check declines the token rather than mistaking "already expired" for "no
1237	// expiry reported". Zero is honoured the same way — it is what an issuer
1238	// computing whole seconds emits for a token with under a second left.
1239	//
1240	// Note this is deliberately NOT identical to changeforge's tokenExpiresAt, which
1241	// reads the same field off the same endpoint: that one collapses non-positive
1242	// values to "unknown". Divergent on purpose (see this doc's paragraph above),
1243	// and they cannot share code — changeforge imports nothing from this repo.
1244	func expiresInToExpiry(raw json.RawMessage, now time.Time) time.Time {
1245		// An absent or explicitly null field means "not reported". json.Unmarshal of
1246		// null returns nil error and leaves the target UNTOUCHED, so without this
1247		// check a null would read as a reported zero, i.e. "already expired".
1248		if len(raw) == 0 || string(raw) == "null" {
1249			return time.Time{}
1250		}
1251		var seconds float64
1252		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &seconds); err != nil {
1253			return time.Time{}
1254		}
1255		switch {
1256		case math.IsNaN(seconds), math.IsInf(seconds, 0):
1257			return time.Time{}
1258		case seconds > maxPlausibleExpiresIn.Seconds():
1259			// Implausible. Report it as unreported rather than clamping to a
1260			// long window: the caller bounds an unknown lifetime tightly.
1261			return time.Time{}
1262		case seconds < -maxPlausibleExpiresIn.Seconds():
1263			return now.Add(-maxPlausibleExpiresIn)
1264		}
1265		return now.Add(time.Duration(seconds * float64(time.Second)))
1266	}

# entire-api — agent notes

Per-jurisdiction Go service: HTTP API + two NATS workers (repo-activity,
user-activity) over two Postgres stores (`repo`, `usr` schemas). See
[README.md](./README.md) for architecture and [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md)
for build/test.

## Conventions an agent must not get wrong

- **Database migrations use a UTC-timestamp version, never a hand-picked
  integer.** Create them with `scripts/new-migration.sh <repo|user> <name>` →
  `internal/store/migrations/<store>/YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_<name>.sql`. goose tracks by
  the filename's version number and silently skips any version `≤` the current
  DB version, so two PRs picking the same next integer (e.g. both `016_…`) make
  one migration vanish with no error. Leave the existing `001…0NN` files as-is.
  Full rationale: [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md#database-migrations).
- **Never renumber or edit a migration that has been merged _and applied_** —
  add a new (timestamped) one. Merged alone is not the test. A migration can sit
  on `main` having never reached a database, which is exactly what happens when
  `migration-check` blocks the deploy that would have applied it. Ask the
  deploy marker — the last commit whose migrations reached a database. Buildkite
  keeps it in SSM, not git: `AWS_PROFILE=nonprod-admin AWS_REGION=us-east-2 aws
  ssm get-parameter --name /entire-api/deployed/staging --query Parameter.Value
  --output text`, then `git ls-tree <sha> internal/store/migrations/<store>/`
  to see whether the file is in that tree. (Do not use `refs/deploy/staging`:
  it no longer moves, and `origin` does not have it.) In it, leave it alone;
  absent from it, restamping it forward
  is the fix, and usually the only one (the deploy stays blocked until the
  version moves). Prod trails staging by one fleet promote PR per green main
  build (`gh pr list -R entirehq/fleet --state all --search "promote <sha7>"`).
  To settle it from a database instead, ask the catalog, not
  `information_schema` (which hides tables the reading role has no grant on) and
  not `goose_activity_repo` (`operator_ro` has no grant on it):
  `SELECT to_regclass('repo.<table>');` for a table, or for a column
  `SELECT attname FROM pg_attribute WHERE attrelid = to_regclass('repo.<table>') AND attname = '<column>';`
  via `AWS_PROFILE=<prod|nonprod-admin> AWS_REGION=<cell> mise run db:connect ro`.
- **A `changeforge.NewServiceForge` reason must be registered in entiredb's Core
  before it works, and registering it takes two edits there.** The reason string
  is a cross-repo contract with no enforcement on either side: Core admits an
  exact `(workload, reason)` pair, and nothing here fails when it doesn't. In
  `entiredb`'s `core/api/sts_token.go` you need **both** a row in
  `githubInstallationTokenCapabilities` *and* the reason added to that
  authority's arm of `validFor` — a row without the `validFor` entry is still
  rejected. Grep entiredb for the reason string in the same change that
  introduces it here.

  This fails silently by design: every service-forge caller is best-effort, so a
  denied mint is logged and swallowed and the feature simply never acts. Two
  shipped dead this way (`runner_checks_failed`, `trail_gate_checks_resync`). One
  was worse than a no-op — `gaterecompute` treats a failed check-run read as
  fail-closed, so the denied mint flipped the checks gate to a **blocking
  `error`**, meaning the resync route broke the gate it exists to repair. If a
  forge-backed feature does nothing in prod and nothing is in the logs, check
  the reason is admitted before reading any further.
- **A trail actor is an account ULID.** A GitHub login is forge data about
  commits, never an actor identity: nothing stores one for an assignee,
  reviewer, approver or message author. One read-side exception: a legacy
  login-only `repo_trails.assignees` element with no account id anywhere
  still renders its stored login (`assigneeActors` in
  `internal/httpapi/changes_types.go`) until those rows are retired. The
  bare-login input arm in `internal/httpapi/trail_actor_refs.go` is a
  deprecation for old CLIs, not a compatibility contract; it goes once
  `trail_actor_resolve_total{kind=github_login}` is flat (ENT-2922).
- **Run `mise run vet`, `mise run lint` before pushing.**
  Integration tests (`mise run test:integration`) need Docker and self-skip
  without `ACTIVITY_TEST_DATABASE_URL`; plain `mise run test` stays unit-only.

## Testing cross-cell behaviour

`internal/multicellular` is the cross-jurisdiction suite — several real cells
(embedded NATS + real Postgres each) driven over real transport; the only CI suite
that's cross-cell, real-transport, and real-store at once. See its README for the DSL.

Add or extend a scenario there when a change affects behaviour that only appears
when ≥2 cells (placements) interact, or depends on an event crossing cells: activity
forwarding (origin / `repo_group` keying, dedup, the `/me` pull gate), settings
fan-out (`settingsrelay` / `settingsconsumer` / `mirrorlifecycle`), placement-

1	package auth
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"errors"
6		"log/slog"
7		"strings"
8		"sync"
9		"time"
10	
11		"golang.org/x/sync/singleflight"
12	)
13	
14	// ApprovalVerdict is the outcome of an account-approval check (COR-940). It
15	// mirrors entire-core's management-plane gate: 403 only on a confirmed deny,
16	// retryable on a lookup failure (COR-631 — an unavailable credential is not a
17	// verdict).
18	type ApprovalVerdict int
19	
20	const (
21		VerdictApproved ApprovalVerdict = iota
22		VerdictWaitlisted
23		VerdictUnavailable
24	)
25	
26	// ErrAccountNotFound is the lookup's signal that no account row exists (a reaped
27	// account) — treated as waitlisted, fail closed. The wiring adapter maps
28	// coreapi's not-found to this so the auth package stays free of the coreapi
29	// import; any other lookup error is unavailable.
30	var ErrAccountNotFound = errors.New("auth: account not found")
31	
32	// serviceAccountPrefix marks machine identities, out of the waitlist by
33	// construction (provisioned by an approved org manager), so the checker approves
34	// them without a lookup — mirroring core's IsServiceAccount carve-out.
35	const serviceAccountPrefix = "svc_"
36	
37	const (
38		defaultApprovalTTL = 60 * time.Second
39		// approvalCacheMax hard-caps the verdict cache. Expiry cleanup happens on read
40		// (see cached), so this only bounds a churn of distinct callers whose entries
41		// are never re-read; a per-region API stays well under it.
42		approvalCacheMax = 16384

1	package ingest
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"errors"
6		"time"
7	
8		"github.com/entirehq/entire-api/internal/coreapi"
9	)
10	
11	// defaultNegativeTTL bounds how long an unresolved pusher stays cached without a
12	// home placement. Short enough that a live ingester recovers the placement once
13	// Core can resolve it (the account-by-id endpoint ships); long enough that a
14	// burst of the same unresolved pusher doesn't re-query Core on every commit.
15	const defaultNegativeTTL = 15 * time.Minute
16	
17	// defaultResolveTTL bounds how long a positive author/pusher resolution stays
18	// cached. Modest, because an identity can change (a pusher's account state, a
19	// verified-email link that reassigns an author's account/login) — a miss just
20	// re-resolves against current Core state, so the TTL only trades a periodic
21	// re-query for staleness, never correctness.
22	const defaultResolveTTL = time.Hour
23	
24	// resolveCacheSize caps the author and pusher resolver LRUs. A region-wide
25	// backfill streams far more distinct emails/ULIDs than a pod needs resident at
26	// once; the bound keeps memory flat while staying large enough to serve the hot
27	// set of a busy cell without thrashing.
28	const resolveCacheSize = 16384
29	
30	// PusherResolver maps a pusher's account ULID to its home placement, caching
31	// results. It is three-valued, mirroring coreapi.AccountByID: an empty id, an
32	// unknown account (ErrNotFound) or one with no placement (ErrNoHome) resolves to
33	// (nil, nil) — PERMANENTLY unattributable, and never a guessed home; a transport
34	// error resolves to (nil, err) and is NOT cached, so the caller naks and
35	// redelivery re-resolves. Before ENT-1816 both collapsed to a bare nil, which
36	// let a Core outage look exactly like a deleted account.
37	//
38	// A positive result caches for resolveTTL and a negative for negativeTTL, both
39	// in a bounded LRU (resolveCacheSize entries) that can never grow without limit
40	// across a region-wide backfill. Resolving at ingest against current account
41	// state can never go stale onto the replayable ref event (nothing about
42	// placement is frozen there), and every expiry/eviction just re-resolves — so a
43	// later Core resolution is always picked up without a restart.
44	// Concurrency-safe; share one across pipeline workers.
45	type PusherResolver struct {
46		core        AccountClient
47		ttl         time.Duration // positive-entry lifetime
48		negativeTTL time.Duration
49	
50		cache *boundedLRU[string, pusherEntry]
51	}
52	
53	type pusherEntry struct {
54		found bool
55		acct  coreapi.Account
56	}
57	
58	// NewPusherResolver builds a resolver over the given account lookup. A nil core
59	// (internal mTLS unconfigured) makes every Resolve return (nil, nil).
60	func NewPusherResolver(core AccountClient) *PusherResolver {
61		return &PusherResolver{
62			core:        core,
63			ttl:         defaultResolveTTL,
64			negativeTTL: defaultNegativeTTL,
65			cache:       newBoundedLRU[string, pusherEntry](resolveCacheSize),
66		}
67	}
68	
69	// Enabled reports whether account resolution is wired at all (an internal-mTLS
70	// Core client is configured). False in local dev / an unconfigured deployment:
71	// there is no authority to ask, so a caller must NOT read a miss as "this
72	// account is unattributable" — see Flow.routableRecipient, which keeps
73	// attributing by id in that case so the publisher's single-region path still
74	// routes the forward locally.
75	func (r *PusherResolver) Enabled() bool { return r != nil && r.core != nil }
76	
77	// Resolve returns the home placement for a pusher ULID. (nil, nil) means
78	// permanently unattributable — no such account, or one with no placement; a
79	// non-nil error means Core is unreachable and the caller should nak. Live cache
80	// hits (positive, or a still-valid negative) skip the Core call.
81	func (r *PusherResolver) Resolve(ctx context.Context, accountID string) (*coreapi.Account, error) {
82		if accountID == "" || r.core == nil {
83			return nil, nil
84		}
85		if acct, hit := r.cached(accountID); hit {
86			return acct, nil
87		}
88	
89		acct, err := r.core.AccountByID(ctx, accountID)
90		if errors.Is(err, coreapi.ErrNotFound) || errors.Is(err, coreapi.ErrNoHome) {
91			// Permanent for this id: cache the miss so a burst of the same deleted
92			// account doesn't re-query Core on every commit.
93			r.cache.put(accountID, pusherEntry{found: false}, r.negativeTTL)
94			return nil, nil
95		}
96		if err != nil {
97			// Transport error: do NOT cache, and hand it back rather than reporting
98			// "unattributable" — the caller naks and redelivery re-resolves. Logging
99			// lives at the caller, which knows which forward is being abandoned.
100			return nil, err
101		}
102		a := *acct
103		r.cache.put(accountID, pusherEntry{found: true, acct: a}, r.ttl)
104		return &a, nil
105	}
106	
107	// cached returns (account, true) on a live hit — a positive entry (nil-safe
108	// copy) or a still-valid negative (nil account). A miss or an expired entry
109	// (positive or negative) returns (nil, false) so the caller re-queries Core;
110	// expiry is enforced by the bounded LRU.
111	func (r *PusherResolver) cached(accountID string) (*coreapi.Account, bool) {
112		e, ok := r.cache.get(accountID)
113		if !ok {
114			return nil, false
115		}
116		if e.found {
117			acct := e.acct // copy; never hand out a pointer into the cache
118			return &acct, true
119		}
120		return nil, true // negative still valid
121	}

95		}
96		if err != nil {
97			// Transport error: do NOT cache, and hand it back rather than reporting
98			// "unattributable" — the caller naks and redelivery re-resolves. Logging
99			// lives at the caller, which knows which forward is being abandoned.
100			return nil, err
101		}
102		a := *acct
103		r.cache.put(accountID, pusherEntry{found: true, acct: a}, r.ttl)
104		return &a, nil
105	}
106	
107	// cached returns (account, true) on a live hit — a positive entry (nil-safe
108	// copy) or a still-valid negative (nil account). A miss or an expired entry
109	// (positive or negative) returns (nil, false) so the caller re-queries Core;
110	// expiry is enforced by the bounded LRU.
111	func (r *PusherResolver) cached(accountID string) (*coreapi.Account, bool) {
112		e, ok := r.cache.get(accountID)
113		if !ok {
114			return nil, false
115		}
116		if e.found {
117			acct := e.acct // copy; never hand out a pointer into the cache
118			return &acct, true
119		}
120		return nil, true // negative still valid
121	}

1	package mirrorjobs
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"crypto/tls"
6		"crypto/x509"
7		"errors"
8		"fmt"
9		"log/slog"
10		"net/http"
11		"os"
12	
13		"connectrpc.com/connect"
14		"github.com/oklog/ulid/v2"
15		"go.opentelemetry.io/contrib/instrumentation/net/http/otelhttp"
16		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel"
17		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute"
18		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/metric"
19	
20		repolookupv1 "github.com/entirehq/mirror-pipeline/gen/proto/repolookup/v1"
21		"github.com/entirehq/mirror-pipeline/gen/proto/repolookup/v1/repolookupv1connect"
22		"github.com/entirehq/mirror-pipeline/pkg/gitjobs"
23	)
24	
25	// ErrMirrorNotFound is returned by MirrorByID when entire-core has no mirror
26	// for the given ULID (or the placement is suspended). Callers treat it as a
27	// benign skip, not a transient error to retry.
28	var ErrMirrorNotFound = errors.New("mirrorjobs: mirror not found")
29	
30	// RepoLookupClient is the subset of the generated Connect client needed by
31	// CoreLookupResolver.
32	type RepoLookupClient interface {
33		LookupByMirror(context.Context, *connect.Request[repolookupv1.LookupByMirrorRequest]) (*connect.Response[repolookupv1.LookupByMirrorResponse], error)
34		LookupMirrorByID(context.Context, *connect.Request[repolookupv1.LookupMirrorByIDRequest]) (*connect.Response[repolookupv1.LookupMirrorByIDResponse], error)
35	}
36	
37	// NewRepoLookupClient builds a Connect-RPC client over the internal mTLS
38	// listener exposed by entire-core.
39	func NewRepoLookupClient(certPath, keyPath, caPath, baseURL string) (repolookupv1connect.RepoLookupClient, error) {
40		if certPath == "" || keyPath == "" || caPath == "" {
41			return nil, errors.New("ENTIRE_INTERNAL_TLS_{CERT,KEY,CA}_FILE all required for repo lookup")
42		}
43		if baseURL == "" {
44			return nil, errors.New("ENTIRE_CORE_INTERNAL_URL is required for repo lookup")
45		}
46	
47		if _, err := tls.LoadX509KeyPair(certPath, keyPath); err != nil {
48			return nil, fmt.Errorf("load tls keypair: %w", err)
49		}
50		caBytes, err := os.ReadFile(caPath) //nolint:gosec // operator-supplied env var, validated non-empty above
51		if err != nil {
52			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read internal CA: %w", err)
53		}
54		caPool := x509.NewCertPool()
55		if !caPool.AppendCertsFromPEM(caBytes) {
56			return nil, errors.New("internal CA PEM: no certs parsed")
57		}
58	
59		dt, ok := http.DefaultTransport.(*http.Transport)
60		if !ok {
61			return nil, errors.New("http.DefaultTransport is not *http.Transport")
62		}
63		tr := dt.Clone()
64		tr.TLSClientConfig = &tls.Config{
65			GetClientCertificate: func(_ *tls.CertificateRequestInfo) (*tls.Certificate, error) {
66				return loadClientCertificate(certPath, keyPath)
67			},
68			RootCAs:    caPool,
69			MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS13,
70		}
71		tr.ForceAttemptHTTP2 = true
72	
73		httpClient := &http.Client{Transport: otelhttp.NewTransport(tr)}
74		return repolookupv1connect.NewRepoLookupClient(httpClient, baseURL), nil
75	}
76	
77	func loadClientCertificate(certFile, keyFile string) (*tls.Certificate, error) {
78		cert, err := tls.LoadX509KeyPair(certFile, keyFile)
79		if err != nil {
80			return nil, err
81		}
82		return &cert, nil
83	}
84	
85	// CoreLookupResolver resolves GitHub mirrors through entire-core RepoLookup.
86	type CoreLookupResolver struct {
87		client RepoLookupClient
88		skips  metric.Int64Counter
89	}
90	
91	// NewCoreLookupResolver returns a RepoLookup-backed route resolver.
92	func NewCoreLookupResolver(client RepoLookupClient) *CoreLookupResolver {
93		// placement_skipped counts placements dropped from a lookup because a
94		// required routing field was blank, tagged by reason — an alertable signal
95		// that entire-core returned unroutable placement data (otherwise only a WARN
96		// log). Built here, after otel setup in main, so it binds to the real meter
97		// provider rather than the startup no-op.
98		skips, _ := otel.Meter("github.com/entirehq/mirror-pipeline/internal/mirrorjobs").
99			Int64Counter("mirrorjobs.placement_skipped",
100				metric.WithDescription("Placements dropped from a repo lookup because a required routing field (cluster_slug or repo_id) was blank or malformed, by reason."))
101		return &CoreLookupResolver{client: client, skips: skips}
102	}
103	
104	// recordSkip increments the placement_skipped counter with a reason label.
105	// Safe when the counter failed to register (nil).
106	func (r *CoreLookupResolver) recordSkip(ctx context.Context, reason string) {
107		if r.skips != nil {
108			r.skips.Add(ctx, 1, metric.WithAttributes(attribute.String("reason", reason)))
109		}
110	}
111	
112	// RoutesForSource resolves a source event into target mirror routes.
113	func (r *CoreLookupResolver) RoutesForSource(ctx context.Context, event SourceEvent) ([]MirrorRoute, error) {
114		if event.Kind != gitjobs.SourceKindGithub {
115			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported source kind %q", event.Kind)
116		}
117	
118		resp, err := r.client.LookupByMirror(ctx, connect.NewRequest(&repolookupv1.LookupByMirrorRequest{
119			Provider:     string(gitjobs.SourceKindGithub),
120			Owner:        event.Owner,
121			Repo:         event.Repo,
122			GithubRepoId: event.GitHubRepoID,
123		}))
124		if err != nil {
125			return nil, fmt.Errorf("repo lookup: %w", err)
126		}
127	
128		placements := resp.Msg.GetPlacements()
129		if len(placements) == 0 {
130			// entire-core has no mirror registered for this source. Surface this
131			// as an Info log so callers (e.g. the fanout consumer) don't have to
132			// each re-discover the case from an empty routes slice.
133			slog.InfoContext(ctx, "repo lookup returned no placements; source has no mirror",
134				slog.String("source_kind", string(event.Kind)),
135				slog.String("source_owner", event.Owner),
136				slog.String("source_repo", event.Repo))
137		}
138		// Placements are unique per cluster for a source: github_repos has a
139		// UNIQUE(lower(owner_login), lower(repo_name)) index (one github_repo_id per
140		// owner/repo) and mirror_repos has UNIQUE(github_repo_id, cluster_slug) (at
141		// most one mirror per cluster). Fan-out memo correctness relies on this — the
142		// engine keys its per-delivery dedup memo on Region()==cluster_slug (see
143		// fanoutengine.Route), so two routes must never share a cluster in one
144		// delivery. If the mirror model ever allows multiple placements per cluster,
145		// give routes a finer memo key.
146		routes := make([]MirrorRoute, 0, len(placements))
147		for _, p := range placements {
148			if p.GetClusterSlug() == "" {
149				slog.WarnContext(ctx, "repo lookup returned empty cluster slug; skipping placement",
150					slog.String("cluster_slug", p.GetClusterSlug()),
151					slog.String("jurisdiction", p.GetJurisdiction()),
152					slog.String("repo_id", p.GetRepoId()),
153					slog.String("source_owner", event.Owner),
154					slog.String("source_repo", event.Repo))
155				r.recordSkip(ctx, "empty_cluster_slug")
156				continue
157			}
158			if p.GetRepoId() == "" {
159				// A blank mirror repo_id is a server-side data problem for THIS
160				// placement only. Skip it (like the empty cluster slug above) so one
161				// bad placement can't fail the whole delivery — a downstream that
162				// validates the target ULID (e.g. trails-fanout) would otherwise
163				// reject the batch as malformed input and drop every placement.
164				slog.WarnContext(ctx, "repo lookup returned empty repo_id; skipping placement",
165					slog.String("cluster_slug", p.GetClusterSlug()),
166					slog.String("jurisdiction", p.GetJurisdiction()),
167					slog.String("source_owner", event.Owner),

30	// RepoLookupClient is the subset of the generated Connect client needed by

37	// NewRepoLookupClient builds a Connect-RPC client over the internal mTLS
38	// listener exposed by entire-core.
39	func NewRepoLookupClient(certPath, keyPath, caPath, baseURL string) (repolookupv1connect.RepoLookupClient, error) {
40		if certPath == "" || keyPath == "" || caPath == "" {
41			return nil, errors.New("ENTIRE_INTERNAL_TLS_{CERT,KEY,CA}_FILE all required for repo lookup")
42		}
43		if baseURL == "" {
44			return nil, errors.New("ENTIRE_CORE_INTERNAL_URL is required for repo lookup")
45		}
46	
47		if _, err := tls.LoadX509KeyPair(certPath, keyPath); err != nil {
48			return nil, fmt.Errorf("load tls keypair: %w", err)
49		}
50		caBytes, err := os.ReadFile(caPath) //nolint:gosec // operator-supplied env var, validated non-empty above
51		if err != nil {
52			return nil, fmt.Errorf("read internal CA: %w", err)
53		}
54		caPool := x509.NewCertPool()
55		if !caPool.AppendCertsFromPEM(caBytes) {
56			return nil, errors.New("internal CA PEM: no certs parsed")
57		}
58	
59		dt, ok := http.DefaultTransport.(*http.Transport)
60		if !ok {
61			return nil, errors.New("http.DefaultTransport is not *http.Transport")
62		}
63		tr := dt.Clone()
64		tr.TLSClientConfig = &tls.Config{
65			GetClientCertificate: func(_ *tls.CertificateRequestInfo) (*tls.Certificate, error) {
66				return loadClientCertificate(certPath, keyPath)
67			},
68			RootCAs:    caPool,
69			MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS13,
70		}
71		tr.ForceAttemptHTTP2 = true
72	
73		httpClient := &http.Client{Transport: otelhttp.NewTransport(tr)}
74		return repolookupv1connect.NewRepoLookupClient(httpClient, baseURL), nil
75	}

77	func loadClientCertificate(certFile, keyFile string) (*tls.Certificate, error) {
78		cert, err := tls.LoadX509KeyPair(certFile, keyFile)
79		if err != nil {
80			return nil, err
81		}
82		return &cert, nil
83	}

91	// NewCoreLookupResolver returns a RepoLookup-backed route resolver.
92	func NewCoreLookupResolver(client RepoLookupClient) *CoreLookupResolver {
93		// placement_skipped counts placements dropped from a lookup because a
94		// required routing field was blank, tagged by reason — an alertable signal
95		// that entire-core returned unroutable placement data (otherwise only a WARN
96		// log). Built here, after otel setup in main, so it binds to the real meter
97		// provider rather than the startup no-op.
98		skips, _ := otel.Meter("github.com/entirehq/mirror-pipeline/internal/mirrorjobs").
99			Int64Counter("mirrorjobs.placement_skipped",
100				metric.WithDescription("Placements dropped from a repo lookup because a required routing field (cluster_slug or repo_id) was blank or malformed, by reason."))
101		return &CoreLookupResolver{client: client, skips: skips}
102	}

104	// recordSkip increments the placement_skipped counter with a reason label.
105	// Safe when the counter failed to register (nil).
106	func (r *CoreLookupResolver) recordSkip(ctx context.Context, reason string) {
107		if r.skips != nil {
108			r.skips.Add(ctx, 1, metric.WithAttributes(attribute.String("reason", reason)))
109		}
110	}

112	// RoutesForSource resolves a source event into target mirror routes.
113	func (r *CoreLookupResolver) RoutesForSource(ctx context.Context, event SourceEvent) ([]MirrorRoute, error) {
114		if event.Kind != gitjobs.SourceKindGithub {
115			return nil, fmt.Errorf("unsupported source kind %q", event.Kind)
116		}
117	
118		resp, err := r.client.LookupByMirror(ctx, connect.NewRequest(&repolookupv1.LookupByMirrorRequest{
119			Provider:     string(gitjobs.SourceKindGithub),
120			Owner:        event.Owner,
121			Repo:         event.Repo,
122			GithubRepoId: event.GitHubRepoID,
123		}))
124		if err != nil {
125			return nil, fmt.Errorf("repo lookup: %w", err)
126		}
127	
128		placements := resp.Msg.GetPlacements()
129		if len(placements) == 0 {
130			// entire-core has no mirror registered for this source. Surface this
131			// as an Info log so callers (e.g. the fanout consumer) don't have to
132			// each re-discover the case from an empty routes slice.
133			slog.InfoContext(ctx, "repo lookup returned no placements; source has no mirror",
134				slog.String("source_kind", string(event.Kind)),
135				slog.String("source_owner", event.Owner),
136				slog.String("source_repo", event.Repo))
137		}
138		// Placements are unique per cluster for a source: github_repos has a
139		// UNIQUE(lower(owner_login), lower(repo_name)) index (one github_repo_id per
140		// owner/repo) and mirror_repos has UNIQUE(github_repo_id, cluster_slug) (at
141		// most one mirror per cluster). Fan-out memo correctness relies on this — the
142		// engine keys its per-delivery dedup memo on Region()==cluster_slug (see
143		// fanoutengine.Route), so two routes must never share a cluster in one
144		// delivery. If the mirror model ever allows multiple placements per cluster,
145		// give routes a finer memo key.
146		routes := make([]MirrorRoute, 0, len(placements))
147		for _, p := range placements {
148			if p.GetClusterSlug() == "" {
149				slog.WarnContext(ctx, "repo lookup returned empty cluster slug; skipping placement",
150					slog.String("cluster_slug", p.GetClusterSlug()),
151					slog.String("jurisdiction", p.GetJurisdiction()),
152					slog.String("repo_id", p.GetRepoId()),
153					slog.String("source_owner", event.Owner),
154					slog.String("source_repo", event.Repo))
155				r.recordSkip(ctx, "empty_cluster_slug")
156				continue
157			}
158			if p.GetRepoId() == "" {
159				// A blank mirror repo_id is a server-side data problem for THIS
160				// placement only. Skip it (like the empty cluster slug above) so one
161				// bad placement can't fail the whole delivery — a downstream that
162				// validates the target ULID (e.g. trails-fanout) would otherwise
163				// reject the batch as malformed input and drop every placement.
164				slog.WarnContext(ctx, "repo lookup returned empty repo_id; skipping placement",
165					slog.String("cluster_slug", p.GetClusterSlug()),
166					slog.String("jurisdiction", p.GetJurisdiction()),
167					slog.String("source_owner", event.Owner),
168					slog.String("source_repo", event.Repo))
169				r.recordSkip(ctx, "empty_repo_id")
170				continue
171			}
172			if _, err := ulid.ParseStrict(p.GetRepoId()); err != nil {
173				// Same per-placement data problem as a blank repo_id, just non-empty:
174				// a malformed ULID would fail trails-fanout's per-placement event
175				// validation and Term-drop the whole delivery for every cell.
176				slog.WarnContext(ctx, "repo lookup returned malformed repo_id; skipping placement",
177					slog.String("repo_id", p.GetRepoId()),
178					slog.String("cluster_slug", p.GetClusterSlug()),
179					slog.String("jurisdiction", p.GetJurisdiction()),
180					slog.String("source_owner", event.Owner),
181					slog.String("source_repo", event.Repo))
182				r.recordSkip(ctx, "invalid_repo_id")
183				continue
184			}
185			routes = append(routes, MirrorRoute{
186				Placement: gitjobs.Placement{
187					Jurisdiction: p.GetJurisdiction(),
188					ClusterID:    p.GetClusterSlug(),
189				},
190				SourceKind: event.Kind,
191				Source: gitjobs.Source{
192					Owner:   event.Owner,
193					Repo:    event.Repo,
194					AuthRef: event.AuthRef,
195				},
196				Target: gitjobs.Target{ULID: p.GetRepoId()},
197			})
198		}
199		return routes, nil
200	}

3	import (
4		"context"
5		"strconv"
6		"sync"
7		"time"
8	
9		"connectrpc.com/connect"
10		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/attribute"
11		"go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace"
12		"golang.org/x/sync/singleflight"
13	
14		repolookupv1 "github.com/entirehq/mirror-pipeline/gen/proto/repolookup/v1"
15	)
16	
17	// defaultLookupTimeout caps each upstream RepoLookup RPC. It applies inside
18	// the singleflight slot on a detached context so one caller cancelling can't
19	// kill an in-flight lookup that other callers are coalesced onto.
20	const defaultLookupTimeout = 10 * time.Second
21	
22	// defaultSweepInterval is how often Run scans the entry map for expired
23	// entries. Lookups already evict on read; the sweeper exists only to drop
24	// one-shot keys that never get re-read so memory stays bounded over the
25	// process lifetime.
26	const defaultSweepInterval = 5 * time.Minute
27	
28	// CachingRepoLookupClient wraps a RepoLookupClient with a read-through in-memory
29	// cache keyed on (provider, owner, repo, github_repo_id).
30	//
31	// Positive responses live for PosTTL; empty ("no placements") responses live
32	// for NegTTL, kept short on purpose — a stale negative entry silently delays
33	// mirror activation when a user wires a new repo in entire-core. A stale
34	// positive entry can also route pushes to a previously-placed cluster for up
35	// to PosTTL after a re-placement, but mirror moves are rare and worst case
36	// we route to the prior cluster set briefly; an outage of the wrong cluster
37	// is far costlier than a few seconds of stale routing.
38	//
39	// Concurrent misses on the same key are coalesced via singleflight so a push
40	// burst on a cold key fans to a single upstream RPC. Errors are never cached.
41	//
42	// The upstream RPC runs on a detached context (the leader's caller cancelling
43	// would otherwise propagate to every coalesced waiter and silently drop a
44	// burst of webhook routes). Each caller selects on its own ctx so an
45	// individual cancellation only affects that caller.
46	//
47	// On error the leader retries once inside the same singleflight slot before
48	// broadcasting, so all coalesced waiters share the retry. Caps upstream
49	// fanout at 2 RPCs per burst regardless of waiter count — a retry done in
50	// the outer code would race against late waiters spawning new singleflight
51	// slots once the first one drains.
52	type CachingRepoLookupClient struct {
53		inner         RepoLookupClient
54		posTTL        time.Duration
55		negTTL        time.Duration
56		lookupTimeout time.Duration
57		sweepInterval time.Duration
58		now           func() time.Time
59	
60		entries sync.Map // map[string]*cacheEntry
61		group   singleflight.Group
62	}
63	
64	type cacheEntry struct {
65		placements []*repolookupv1.Placement
66		expiresAt  time.Time
67	}
68	
69	// lookupOutcome is the value singleflight broadcasts to all coalesced
70	// waiters: the placements plus whether the leader had to retry. Carrying
71	// retried through the singleflight result is what makes all waiters see the
72	// same telemetry (a shared call shares its outcome).
73	type lookupOutcome struct {
74		placements []*repolookupv1.Placement
75		retried    bool
76	}
77	
78	// NewCachingRepoLookupClient builds a cache around inner. A zero posTTL or
79	// negTTL disables caching for that class of response (the call always falls
80	// through to inner).
81	func NewCachingRepoLookupClient(inner RepoLookupClient, posTTL, negTTL time.Duration) *CachingRepoLookupClient {
82		return &CachingRepoLookupClient{
83			inner:         inner,
84			posTTL:        posTTL,
85			negTTL:        negTTL,
86			lookupTimeout: defaultLookupTimeout,
87			sweepInterval: defaultSweepInterval,
88			now:           time.Now,
89		}
90	}
91	
92	func (c *CachingRepoLookupClient) LookupByMirror(ctx context.Context, req *connect.Request[repolookupv1.LookupByMirrorRequest]) (*connect.Response[repolookupv1.LookupByMirrorResponse], error) {
93		span := trace.SpanFromContext(ctx)
94		key := cacheKey(req.Msg)
95		if entry, ok := c.lookup(key); ok {
96			span.SetAttributes(
97				attribute.String("mirrorjobs.lookup.cache", "hit"),
98				attribute.Int("mirrorjobs.lookup.placements", len(entry.placements)),
99			)
100			return connect.NewResponse(&repolookupv1.LookupByMirrorResponse{Placements: entry.placements}), nil
101		}
102	
103		// Retry once inside the singleflight slot so every coalesced waiter
104		// shares the retry. Doing it in the outer code instead would race: late
105		// waiters could spawn new singleflight slots once the first one drained,
106		// turning the cap into N+1 RPCs on a fast retry. We can't read Shared
107		// from inside the closure, so lone callers retry too — the cost is
108		// bounded (2x on lone errors) and worth it for a webhook ingest where
109		// each unretried error is a dropped push.
110		attempt := func() (*connect.Response[repolookupv1.LookupByMirrorResponse], error) {
111			// WithoutCancel detaches cancellation/deadline so leader cancellation
112			// can't propagate to coalesced waiters, while preserving ctx values
113			// (the OTel span, baggage, logger) so the upstream HTTP span still
114			// chains under the current trace.
115			aCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), c.lookupTimeout)
116			defer cancel()
117			return c.inner.LookupByMirror(aCtx, req)
118		}
119	
120		doLookup := func() (any, error) {
121			resp, err := attempt()
122			retried := false
123			if err != nil {
124				retried = true
125				resp, err = attempt()
126				if err != nil {
127					return nil, err
128				}
129			}
130			placements := resp.Msg.GetPlacements()
131			c.store(key, placements)
132			return &lookupOutcome{placements: placements, retried: retried}, nil
133		}
134	
135		res, err := c.awaitLookup(ctx, key, doLookup)
136		if err != nil {
137			return nil, err
138		}
139		if res.Err != nil {
140			return nil, res.Err
141		}
142	
143		out, _ := res.Val.(*lookupOutcome)
144		span.SetAttributes(
145			attribute.String("mirrorjobs.lookup.cache", "miss"),
146			attribute.Bool("mirrorjobs.lookup.cache.coalesced", res.Shared),
147			attribute.Bool("mirrorjobs.lookup.cache.retried", out.retried),
148			attribute.Int("mirrorjobs.lookup.placements", len(out.placements)),
149		)
150		return connect.NewResponse(&repolookupv1.LookupByMirrorResponse{Placements: out.placements}), nil
151	}
152	
153	// LookupMirrorByID passes through to the inner client uncached. The by-ULID
154	// lookup is one-shot per mirror creation (a low-volume control-plane event),
155	// not a hot webhook path, so the read-through cache that fronts LookupByMirror
156	// buys nothing here — and a mirror ULID maps to immutable upstream coords, so
157	// there is no staleness window worth managing either.
158	func (c *CachingRepoLookupClient) LookupMirrorByID(ctx context.Context, req *connect.Request[repolookupv1.LookupMirrorByIDRequest]) (*connect.Response[repolookupv1.LookupMirrorByIDResponse], error) {
159		return c.inner.LookupMirrorByID(ctx, req)
160	}
161	
162	// awaitLookup runs the singleflight call and blocks until either the result
163	// arrives or the caller's ctx is canceled. On ctx cancellation the
164	// singleflight slot keeps running and will still populate the cache for the
165	// next caller.
166	func (c *CachingRepoLookupClient) awaitLookup(ctx context.Context, key string, fn func() (any, error)) (singleflight.Result, error) {
167		select {
168		case res := <-c.group.DoChan(key, fn):
169			return res, nil
170		case <-ctx.Done():
171			return singleflight.Result{}, ctx.Err()
172		}
173	}

175	// Run periodically evicts expired entries until ctx is canceled. The cache
176	// works without it (lookups evict on read), but a long-running process that
177	// sees a long tail of one-shot keys would otherwise grow without bound.
178	func (c *CachingRepoLookupClient) Run(ctx context.Context) {
179		ticker := time.NewTicker(c.sweepInterval)
180		defer ticker.Stop()
181		for {
182			select {
183			case <-ctx.Done():
184				return
185			case <-ticker.C:
186				c.sweep()
187			}
188		}
189	}
190	
191	func (c *CachingRepoLookupClient) sweep() {
192		now := c.now()
193		c.entries.Range(func(k, v any) bool {
194			entry, ok := v.(*cacheEntry)
195			if !ok {
196				c.entries.Delete(k)
197				return true
198			}
199			if !now.Before(entry.expiresAt) {
200				// CompareAndDelete so a concurrent writer that re-stored a
201				// fresh entry under the same key between our Range read and
202				// the delete isn't clobbered.
203				c.entries.CompareAndDelete(k, v)
204			}
205			return true
206		})
207	}

209	func (c *CachingRepoLookupClient) store(key string, placements []*repolookupv1.Placement) {
210		ttl := c.posTTL
211		if len(placements) == 0 {
212			ttl = c.negTTL
213		}
214		if ttl > 0 {
215			c.entries.Store(key, &cacheEntry{
216				placements: placements,
217				expiresAt:  c.now().Add(ttl),
218			})
219		}
220	}
221	
222	func (c *CachingRepoLookupClient) lookup(key string) (*cacheEntry, bool) {
223		v, ok := c.entries.Load(key)
224		if !ok {
225			return nil, false
226		}
227		entry, ok := v.(*cacheEntry)
228		if !ok {
229			return nil, false
230		}
231		if !c.now().Before(entry.expiresAt) {
232			c.entries.Delete(key)
233			return nil, false
234		}
235		return entry, true
236	}

240	// placements must never answer the other's lookup (ENT-2822).

26	// NativeMirrorLookupClient is the subset of the generated Connect client
27	// needed by NativeMirrorResolver. Kept separate from RepoLookupClient so the
28	// GitHub-webhook resolver and its fakes don't grow a method they never call.
29	type NativeMirrorLookupClient interface {
30		LookupNativeMirrorsByRepoID(context.Context, *connect.Request[repolookupv1.LookupNativeMirrorsByRepoIDRequest]) (*connect.Response[repolookupv1.LookupNativeMirrorsByRepoIDResponse], error)

33	// NativeMirrorResolution is one resolved ref event: the group's git-data home
34	// cluster (the loop-prevention key — the caller drops the event unless its
35	// local cluster is the home) and one sync route per serving mirror.
36	type NativeMirrorResolution struct {
37		HomeClusterID string
38		Routes        []MirrorRoute
39		// NamespaceRoutes replicate only refs/heads/entire/native/* (COR-1566)
40		// onto the group's namespace mirrors — GitHub placements that own the
41		// rest of their ref state. Core populates namespace mirrors only for
42		// GitHub groups, which have no native mirrors, so this is never
43		// non-empty at the same time as Routes; the caller filters the event's
44		// ref name against the namespace before publishing these.

49	// native-mirror sync routes through entire-core
50	// RepoLookup.LookupNativeMirrorsByRepoID.

52		client NativeMirrorLookupClient
53		skips  metric.Int64Counter
54	}

56	// NewNativeMirrorResolver returns a lookup-backed native-mirror route
57	// resolver. The placement_skipped counter is shared (by name) with
58	// CoreLookupResolver — same signal, same dashboards: entire-core returned
59	// unroutable placement data.
60	func NewNativeMirrorResolver(client NativeMirrorLookupClient) *NativeMirrorResolver {
61		skips, _ := otel.Meter("github.com/entirehq/mirror-pipeline/internal/mirrorjobs").
62			Int64Counter("mirrorjobs.placement_skipped",
63				metric.WithDescription("Placements dropped from a repo lookup because a required routing field (cluster_slug or repo_id) was blank or malformed, by reason."))
64		return &NativeMirrorResolver{client: client, skips: skips}

67	func (r *NativeMirrorResolver) recordSkip(ctx context.Context, reason string) {
68		if r.skips != nil {

73	// validateNativeMirrorLookupResponse checks the two response invariants a
74	// delivery cannot proceed without: a home placement with a cluster slug (the
75	// loop-prevention key) and, when any routable mirror exists, a source URL
76	// (the sync job's fetch source). Shared by NativeMirrorRoutes (which fails
77	// the delivery on a violation → Nak → redelivery until Core is fixed) and
78	// the caching client (which must NOT store a violating response — a cached
79	// one would keep failing redeliveries for a full TTL after the Core-side
80	// fix). Per-placement problems are deliberately NOT here: a single malformed
81	// placement only skips that route, so it must not block caching either.
82	func validateNativeMirrorLookupResponse(resp *repolookupv1.LookupNativeMirrorsByRepoIDResponse) error {
83		if resp.GetHome().GetClusterSlug() == "" {
84			return errors.New("home placement has no cluster slug")
85		}
86		if resp.GetSourceUrl() == "" &&
87			(slices.ContainsFunc(resp.GetNativeMirrors(), routableNativeMirror) ||
88				slices.ContainsFunc(resp.GetNamespaceMirrors(), routableNativeMirror)) {
89			return fmt.Errorf("home cluster %s has no internal source URL registered", resp.GetHome().GetClusterSlug())
90		}

95	// NativeMirrorRoutes's per-placement validation and become a route.
96	func routableNativeMirror(p *repolookupv1.Placement) bool {

98			return false
99		}
100		_, err := ulid.ParseStrict(p.GetRepoId())
101		return err == nil

104	// NativeMirrorRoutes resolves the repo id carried by a ref event (any
105	// placement of the repo — the home primary, or a mirror echoing a worker
106	// push) to its group's home cluster, one sync route per serving native
107	// mirror, and one namespace route per namespace mirror. Both route sets
108	// empty is normal — a repo with no mirrors, i.e. every repo today.
109	//
110	// Mirrors of either kind are unique per cluster (UNIQUE(repo_group_id,
111	// cluster_slug) on native_mirrors; one mirror_repos row per cluster in a
112	// GitHub group), so two routes never share a Region() in one delivery — the
113	// fan-out engine's route-memo correctness bound.
114	//
115	// Errors: ErrNativeRepoNotFound for an unknown repo id (benign skip — the
116	// repo was deleted); a plain error otherwise (transient — the caller Naks so
117	// JetStream redelivers). A response whose home placement is missing its
118	// cluster slug, or whose source_url is empty while serving mirrors exist, is
119	// also a plain error: both are server-side data/config problems (an
120	// unregistered internal URL for the home cluster) that an operator fix
121	// heals, and dropping the event instead would silently strand the mirrors
122	// until the next push.
123	func (r *NativeMirrorResolver) NativeMirrorRoutes(ctx context.Context, repoID string) (NativeMirrorResolution, error) {
124		if repoID == "" {
125			return NativeMirrorResolution{}, errors.New("repo id is required")
126		}
127	
128		resp, err := r.client.LookupNativeMirrorsByRepoID(ctx, connect.NewRequest(&repolookupv1.LookupNativeMirrorsByRepoIDRequest{
129			RepoId: repoID,
130		}))
131		if err != nil {
132			if connect.CodeOf(err) == connect.CodeNotFound {
133				return NativeMirrorResolution{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrNativeRepoNotFound, repoID)
134			}
135			return NativeMirrorResolution{}, fmt.Errorf("native mirror lookup %s: %w", repoID, err)
136		}
137	
138		if err := validateNativeMirrorLookupResponse(resp.Msg); err != nil {
139			return NativeMirrorResolution{}, fmt.Errorf("native mirror lookup %s: %w", repoID, err)
140		}
141		return NativeMirrorResolution{
142			HomeClusterID:   resp.Msg.GetHome().GetClusterSlug(),
143			Routes:          r.routesFor(ctx, repoID, gitjobs.SourceKindEntireDB, resp.Msg.GetSourceUrl(), resp.Msg.GetNativeMirrors()),
144			NamespaceRoutes: r.routesFor(ctx, repoID, gitjobs.SourceKindEntireDBNamespace, resp.Msg.GetSourceUrl(), resp.Msg.GetNamespaceMirrors()),
145		}, nil
146	}

148	// routesFor turns one placement list into sync routes of the given kind,
149	// skipping (and counting) placements Core returned without the routing
150	// fields a job needs.
151	func (r *NativeMirrorResolver) routesFor(ctx context.Context, repoID string, kind gitjobs.SourceKind, sourceURL string, mirrors []*repolookupv1.Placement) []MirrorRoute {
152		routes := make([]MirrorRoute, 0, len(mirrors))
153		for _, p := range mirrors {
154			if p.GetClusterSlug() == "" {
155				slog.WarnContext(ctx, "native mirror lookup returned empty cluster slug; skipping placement",
156					slog.String("jurisdiction", p.GetJurisdiction()),
157					slog.String("mirror_repo_id", p.GetRepoId()),
158					slog.String("repo_id", repoID))
159				r.recordSkip(ctx, "empty_cluster_slug")
160				continue
161			}
162			if p.GetRepoId() == "" {
163				slog.WarnContext(ctx, "native mirror lookup returned empty repo_id; skipping placement",
164					slog.String("cluster_slug", p.GetClusterSlug()),
165					slog.String("jurisdiction", p.GetJurisdiction()),
166					slog.String("repo_id", repoID))
167				r.recordSkip(ctx, "empty_repo_id")
168				continue
169			}
170			if _, err := ulid.ParseStrict(p.GetRepoId()); err != nil {
171				slog.WarnContext(ctx, "native mirror lookup returned malformed repo_id; skipping placement",
172					slog.String("mirror_repo_id", p.GetRepoId()),
173					slog.String("cluster_slug", p.GetClusterSlug()),
174					slog.String("jurisdiction", p.GetJurisdiction()),
175					slog.String("repo_id", repoID))
176				r.recordSkip(ctx, "invalid_repo_id")
177				continue
178			}
179			routes = append(routes, MirrorRoute{
180				Placement: gitjobs.Placement{
181					Jurisdiction: p.GetJurisdiction(),
182					ClusterID:    p.GetClusterSlug(),
183				},
184				SourceKind: kind,
185				Source:     gitjobs.Source{URL: sourceURL},
186				Target:     gitjobs.Target{ULID: p.GetRepoId()},
187			})
188		}
189		return routes
190	}

17	// defaultLookupTimeout caps each upstream RepoLookup RPC. It applies inside
18	// the singleflight slot on a detached context so one caller cancelling can't
19	// kill an in-flight lookup that other callers are coalesced onto.
20	const defaultLookupTimeout = 10 * time.Second
21	
22	// defaultSweepInterval is how often Run scans the entry map for expired
23	// entries. Lookups already evict on read; the sweeper exists only to drop
24	// one-shot keys that never get re-read so memory stays bounded over the
25	// process lifetime.
26	const defaultSweepInterval = 5 * time.Minute

28	// CachingRepoLookupClient wraps a RepoLookupClient with a read-through in-memory
29	// cache keyed on (provider, owner, repo, github_repo_id).
30	//
31	// Positive responses live for PosTTL; empty ("no placements") responses live
32	// for NegTTL, kept short on purpose — a stale negative entry silently delays
33	// mirror activation when a user wires a new repo in entire-core. A stale
34	// positive entry can also route pushes to a previously-placed cluster for up
35	// to PosTTL after a re-placement, but mirror moves are rare and worst case
36	// we route to the prior cluster set briefly; an outage of the wrong cluster
37	// is far costlier than a few seconds of stale routing.
38	//
39	// Concurrent misses on the same key are coalesced via singleflight so a push
40	// burst on a cold key fans to a single upstream RPC. Errors are never cached.
41	//
42	// The upstream RPC runs on a detached context (the leader's caller cancelling
43	// would otherwise propagate to every coalesced waiter and silently drop a
44	// burst of webhook routes). Each caller selects on its own ctx so an
45	// individual cancellation only affects that caller.
46	//
47	// On error the leader retries once inside the same singleflight slot before
48	// broadcasting, so all coalesced waiters share the retry. Caps upstream
49	// fanout at 2 RPCs per burst regardless of waiter count — a retry done in
50	// the outer code would race against late waiters spawning new singleflight
51	// slots once the first one drains.
52	type CachingRepoLookupClient struct {
53		inner         RepoLookupClient
54		posTTL        time.Duration
55		negTTL        time.Duration
56		lookupTimeout time.Duration
57		sweepInterval time.Duration
58		now           func() time.Time
59	
60		entries sync.Map // map[string]*cacheEntry
61		group   singleflight.Group
62	}
63	
64	type cacheEntry struct {
65		placements []*repolookupv1.Placement
66		expiresAt  time.Time
67	}
68	
69	// lookupOutcome is the value singleflight broadcasts to all coalesced
70	// waiters: the placements plus whether the leader had to retry. Carrying
71	// retried through the singleflight result is what makes all waiters see the
72	// same telemetry (a shared call shares its outcome).
73	type lookupOutcome struct {
74		placements []*repolookupv1.Placement
75		retried    bool
76	}
77	
78	// NewCachingRepoLookupClient builds a cache around inner. A zero posTTL or
79	// negTTL disables caching for that class of response (the call always falls
80	// through to inner).
81	func NewCachingRepoLookupClient(inner RepoLookupClient, posTTL, negTTL time.Duration) *CachingRepoLookupClient {
82		return &CachingRepoLookupClient{
83			inner:         inner,
84			posTTL:        posTTL,
85			negTTL:        negTTL,
86			lookupTimeout: defaultLookupTimeout,
87			sweepInterval: defaultSweepInterval,
88			now:           time.Now,
89		}
90	}

92	func (c *CachingRepoLookupClient) LookupByMirror(ctx context.Context, req *connect.Request[repolookupv1.LookupByMirrorRequest]) (*connect.Response[repolookupv1.LookupByMirrorResponse], error) {
93		span := trace.SpanFromContext(ctx)
94		key := cacheKey(req.Msg)
95		if entry, ok := c.lookup(key); ok {
96			span.SetAttributes(
97				attribute.String("mirrorjobs.lookup.cache", "hit"),
98				attribute.Int("mirrorjobs.lookup.placements", len(entry.placements)),
99			)
100			return connect.NewResponse(&repolookupv1.LookupByMirrorResponse{Placements: entry.placements}), nil
101		}
102	
103		// Retry once inside the singleflight slot so every coalesced waiter
104		// shares the retry. Doing it in the outer code instead would race: late
105		// waiters could spawn new singleflight slots once the first one drained,
106		// turning the cap into N+1 RPCs on a fast retry. We can't read Shared
107		// from inside the closure, so lone callers retry too — the cost is
108		// bounded (2x on lone errors) and worth it for a webhook ingest where
109		// each unretried error is a dropped push.
110		attempt := func() (*connect.Response[repolookupv1.LookupByMirrorResponse], error) {
111			// WithoutCancel detaches cancellation/deadline so leader cancellation
112			// can't propagate to coalesced waiters, while preserving ctx values
113			// (the OTel span, baggage, logger) so the upstream HTTP span still
114			// chains under the current trace.
115			aCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), c.lookupTimeout)
116			defer cancel()
117			return c.inner.LookupByMirror(aCtx, req)
118		}
119	
120		doLookup := func() (any, error) {
121			resp, err := attempt()
122			retried := false
123			if err != nil {
124				retried = true
125				resp, err = attempt()
126				if err != nil {
127					return nil, err
128				}
129			}
130			placements := resp.Msg.GetPlacements()
131			c.store(key, placements)
132			return &lookupOutcome{placements: placements, retried: retried}, nil
133		}
134	
135		res, err := c.awaitLookup(ctx, key, doLookup)
136		if err != nil {
137			return nil, err
138		}
139		if res.Err != nil {
140			return nil, res.Err
141		}
142	
143		out, _ := res.Val.(*lookupOutcome)
144		span.SetAttributes(
145			attribute.String("mirrorjobs.lookup.cache", "miss"),
146			attribute.Bool("mirrorjobs.lookup.cache.coalesced", res.Shared),
147			attribute.Bool("mirrorjobs.lookup.cache.retried", out.retried),
148			attribute.Int("mirrorjobs.lookup.placements", len(out.placements)),
149		)
150		return connect.NewResponse(&repolookupv1.LookupByMirrorResponse{Placements: out.placements}), nil
151	}

157	// there is no staleness window worth managing either.

159		return c.inner.LookupMirrorByID(ctx, req)
160	}

183			case <-ctx.Done():
184				return
185			case <-ticker.C:

187			}
188		}
189	}

36	type NativeMirrorResolution struct {
37		HomeClusterID string
38		Routes        []MirrorRoute
39		// NamespaceRoutes replicate only refs/heads/entire/native/* (COR-1566)
40		// onto the group's namespace mirrors — GitHub placements that own the
41		// rest of their ref state. Core populates namespace mirrors only for
42		// GitHub groups, which have no native mirrors, so this is never
43		// non-empty at the same time as Routes; the caller filters the event's
44		// ref name against the namespace before publishing these.
45		NamespaceRoutes []MirrorRoute
46	}
47	
48	// NativeMirrorResolver resolves repo ULIDs from repo_refs_v1 events into
49	// native-mirror sync routes through entire-core
50	// RepoLookup.LookupNativeMirrorsByRepoID.
51	type NativeMirrorResolver struct {
52		client NativeMirrorLookupClient
53		skips  metric.Int64Counter
54	}
55	
56	// NewNativeMirrorResolver returns a lookup-backed native-mirror route
57	// resolver. The placement_skipped counter is shared (by name) with
58	// CoreLookupResolver — same signal, same dashboards: entire-core returned
59	// unroutable placement data.
60	func NewNativeMirrorResolver(client NativeMirrorLookupClient) *NativeMirrorResolver {
61		skips, _ := otel.Meter("github.com/entirehq/mirror-pipeline/internal/mirrorjobs").
62			Int64Counter("mirrorjobs.placement_skipped",
63				metric.WithDescription("Placements dropped from a repo lookup because a required routing field (cluster_slug or repo_id) was blank or malformed, by reason."))
64		return &NativeMirrorResolver{client: client, skips: skips}
65	}
66	
67	func (r *NativeMirrorResolver) recordSkip(ctx context.Context, reason string) {
68		if r.skips != nil {
69			r.skips.Add(ctx, 1, metric.WithAttributes(attribute.String("reason", reason)))
70		}
71	}
72	
73	// validateNativeMirrorLookupResponse checks the two response invariants a
74	// delivery cannot proceed without: a home placement with a cluster slug (the
75	// loop-prevention key) and, when any routable mirror exists, a source URL
76	// (the sync job's fetch source). Shared by NativeMirrorRoutes (which fails
77	// the delivery on a violation → Nak → redelivery until Core is fixed) and
78	// the caching client (which must NOT store a violating response — a cached
79	// one would keep failing redeliveries for a full TTL after the Core-side
80	// fix). Per-placement problems are deliberately NOT here: a single malformed
81	// placement only skips that route, so it must not block caching either.
82	func validateNativeMirrorLookupResponse(resp *repolookupv1.LookupNativeMirrorsByRepoIDResponse) error {
83		if resp.GetHome().GetClusterSlug() == "" {
84			return errors.New("home placement has no cluster slug")
85		}
86		if resp.GetSourceUrl() == "" &&
87			(slices.ContainsFunc(resp.GetNativeMirrors(), routableNativeMirror) ||
88				slices.ContainsFunc(resp.GetNamespaceMirrors(), routableNativeMirror)) {
89			return fmt.Errorf("home cluster %s has no internal source URL registered", resp.GetHome().GetClusterSlug())
90		}
91		return nil
92	}
93	
94	// routableNativeMirror reports whether a placement would survive
95	// NativeMirrorRoutes's per-placement validation and become a route.
96	func routableNativeMirror(p *repolookupv1.Placement) bool {
97		if p.GetClusterSlug() == "" || p.GetRepoId() == "" {
98			return false
99		}
100		_, err := ulid.ParseStrict(p.GetRepoId())
101		return err == nil
102	}
103	
104	// NativeMirrorRoutes resolves the repo id carried by a ref event (any
105	// placement of the repo — the home primary, or a mirror echoing a worker
106	// push) to its group's home cluster, one sync route per serving native
107	// mirror, and one namespace route per namespace mirror. Both route sets
108	// empty is normal — a repo with no mirrors, i.e. every repo today.
109	//
110	// Mirrors of either kind are unique per cluster (UNIQUE(repo_group_id,
111	// cluster_slug) on native_mirrors; one mirror_repos row per cluster in a
112	// GitHub group), so two routes never share a Region() in one delivery — the
113	// fan-out engine's route-memo correctness bound.
114	//
115	// Errors: ErrNativeRepoNotFound for an unknown repo id (benign skip — the
116	// repo was deleted); a plain error otherwise (transient — the caller Naks so
117	// JetStream redelivers). A response whose home placement is missing its
118	// cluster slug, or whose source_url is empty while serving mirrors exist, is
119	// also a plain error: both are server-side data/config problems (an
120	// unregistered internal URL for the home cluster) that an operator fix
121	// heals, and dropping the event instead would silently strand the mirrors
122	// until the next push.
123	func (r *NativeMirrorResolver) NativeMirrorRoutes(ctx context.Context, repoID string) (NativeMirrorResolution, error) {
124		if repoID == "" {
125			return NativeMirrorResolution{}, errors.New("repo id is required")
126		}
127	
128		resp, err := r.client.LookupNativeMirrorsByRepoID(ctx, connect.NewRequest(&repolookupv1.LookupNativeMirrorsByRepoIDRequest{
129			RepoId: repoID,
130		}))
131		if err != nil {
132			if connect.CodeOf(err) == connect.CodeNotFound {
133				return NativeMirrorResolution{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", ErrNativeRepoNotFound, repoID)
134			}
135			return NativeMirrorResolution{}, fmt.Errorf("native mirror lookup %s: %w", repoID, err)
136		}
137	
138		if err := validateNativeMirrorLookupResponse(resp.Msg); err != nil {
139			return NativeMirrorResolution{}, fmt.Errorf("native mirror lookup %s: %w", repoID, err)
140		}
141		return NativeMirrorResolution{
142			HomeClusterID:   resp.Msg.GetHome().GetClusterSlug(),
143			Routes:          r.routesFor(ctx, repoID, gitjobs.SourceKindEntireDB, resp.Msg.GetSourceUrl(), resp.Msg.GetNativeMirrors()),
144			NamespaceRoutes: r.routesFor(ctx, repoID, gitjobs.SourceKindEntireDBNamespace, resp.Msg.GetSourceUrl(), resp.Msg.GetNamespaceMirrors()),
145		}, nil
146	}
147	
148	// routesFor turns one placement list into sync routes of the given kind,
149	// skipping (and counting) placements Core returned without the routing
150	// fields a job needs.
151	func (r *NativeMirrorResolver) routesFor(ctx context.Context, repoID string, kind gitjobs.SourceKind, sourceURL string, mirrors []*repolookupv1.Placement) []MirrorRoute {
152		routes := make([]MirrorRoute, 0, len(mirrors))
153		for _, p := range mirrors {
154			if p.GetClusterSlug() == "" {
155				slog.WarnContext(ctx, "native mirror lookup returned empty cluster slug; skipping placement",
156					slog.String("jurisdiction", p.GetJurisdiction()),
157					slog.String("mirror_repo_id", p.GetRepoId()),
158					slog.String("repo_id", repoID))
159				r.recordSkip(ctx, "empty_cluster_slug")
160				continue
161			}
162			if p.GetRepoId() == "" {
163				slog.WarnContext(ctx, "native mirror lookup returned empty repo_id; skipping placement",
164					slog.String("cluster_slug", p.GetClusterSlug()),
165					slog.String("jurisdiction", p.GetJurisdiction()),
166					slog.String("repo_id", repoID))
167				r.recordSkip(ctx, "empty_repo_id")
168				continue
169			}
170			if _, err := ulid.ParseStrict(p.GetRepoId()); err != nil {
171				slog.WarnContext(ctx, "native mirror lookup returned malformed repo_id; skipping placement",
172					slog.String("mirror_repo_id", p.GetRepoId()),
173					slog.String("cluster_slug", p.GetClusterSlug()),
174					slog.String("jurisdiction", p.GetJurisdiction()),
175					slog.String("repo_id", repoID))
176				r.recordSkip(ctx, "invalid_repo_id")
177				continue
178			}
179			routes = append(routes, MirrorRoute{
180				Placement: gitjobs.Placement{
181					Jurisdiction: p.GetJurisdiction(),
182					ClusterID:    p.GetClusterSlug(),
183				},
184				SourceKind: kind,
185				Source:     gitjobs.Source{URL: sourceURL},
186				Target:     gitjobs.Target{ULID: p.GetRepoId()},
187			})
188		}
189		return routes
190	}
