1	# entire-core read locality in the multi-region global CockroachDB
2	
3	Status: Accepted
4	
5	Tracking: [COR-371](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-371)
6	
7	## TLDR
8	
9	`POST /oauth/token` in EU is far slower than US (EU p50 ~553ms in the
10	handler / ~789ms end-to-end vs US ~30ms) because the token-exchange path
11	issues a handful of CockroachDB reads strictly in series, and each read
12	against the **global** pool is a cross-Atlantic round trip from the
13	Frankfurt pod to the range leaseholder in Ohio (the global cluster's
14	primary region). Measured directly: an EU read of the global cluster is
15	~105ms; an EU read of the regional EU cluster is ~4ms.
16	
17	The fix is read locality, achieved **without `GLOBAL` tables**:
18	
19	- **`signing_keys` — regionalised** (already shipped, COR-378/382/415).
20	  Each jurisdiction mints and serves its own keys from its regional pool,
21	  so the two per-request signing-key reads are now ~4ms local reads
22	  instead of cross-Atlantic hops. This is the single biggest realised win
23	  and the reason an earlier "make `signing_keys` `GLOBAL`" plan was
24	  dropped.
25	- **`clusters` — in-process cached.** The cluster registry is near-static
26	  fixture data; an in-process TTL cache (`cluster.Store.WithCacheTTL`,
27	  mirroring the existing signing-key cache) removes the read from the hot
28	  path after the first lookup. No table-locality change.
29	- **mirror-URL resolution and GitHub-identity mapping — follower reads**
30	  with **fresh-fallback-on-error**, so the staleness-tolerant per-request
31	  lookups read from the local replica (~4ms) while clone-on-create still
32	  works.
33	- **The authorisation decision (`github_user_repo_access`, and the
34	  `github_repos.is_private` flag it depends on) stays a fresh
35	  leaseholder read** — revocation correctness forbids staleness. This is
36	  the irreducible residual: ~2 cross-region reads (~210ms) on a pull in
37	  EU; a push drops the redundant visibility read, leaving ~1 (~105ms).
38	
39	No `GLOBAL` table, no multi-region-SQL DDL runbook, no reconcile rework.
40	The CockroachDB `entirecore` database is left exactly as it is.
41	
42	## Context
43	
44	Investigation on 2026-05-29 (Honeycomb `entire.io` / `entire-core`),
45	re-confirmed 2026-06-16. `POST /oauth/token` latency by region:
46	
47	| region | p50 (May baseline) | p50 (2026-06-16, 7d) | p95 | p99 |
48	|--------|------|------|-----|-----|
49	| us-east-2 (primary) | 199ms | **25ms** (e2e) / 30ms (handler) | 56ms | 88ms |
50	| eu-central-1 | 1030ms | **789ms** (e2e) / 553ms (handler) | 1181ms | 1219ms |
51	
52	EU is ~2% of token volume (~947 handler calls / 7d) but owns essentially
53	the entire latency tail. A representative EU trace is a series of `client`
54	DB spans running back-to-back with near-zero overlap, each a clean
55	multiple of the ~100ms Frankfurt↔Ohio RTT.
56	
57	**The mechanism, measured directly.** Splitting EU (`eu-central-1`) DB
58	reads by the database host they hit (7d):
59	
60	| EU read target | p50 | p99 | reads/7d |
61	|----------------|-----|-----|----------|
62	| `entire-core-prod-global` (Ohio leaseholder) | **104.8ms** | 310ms | 1,559 |
63	| `entire-core-prod-eu` (regional, in-region) | **4.0ms** | 25ms | 703 |
64	
65	This is the whole problem in two rows: reads on the **global** pool cost
66	a ~105ms Atlantic hop from EU; reads on the **regional** pool are local.
67	It also confirms the signing-key regionalisation landed — those reads are
68	now in the 4ms bucket, off the hot path. What remains slow in EU is the
69	set of reads still on the global pool: `clusters`, the
70	`github_mirror_repo_urls → mirror_repos → github_repos` JOIN, `handles`,
71	`github_repos` (`is_private`), and `github_user_repo_access`.
72	
73	The global cluster is `entire-core-prod-global` (CockroachDB v25.4.10,
74	Cloud **Standard**, AWS, multi-region: Frankfurt `eu-central-1`, Ohio
75	`us-east-2` **PRIMARY**, Oregon `us-west-2`). Two facts pin the cause:
76	
77	- **The EU pod's SQL gateway is local.** A `BEGIN` (which touches no
78	  leaseholder) from `entire-core-regional-eu` against the global cluster
79	  is ~1.7ms — the region-less DSN host geo-routes EU pods to a Frankfurt
80	  gateway. The connection is *not* crossing the Atlantic.
81	- **The leaseholders are in Ohio.** The global tables are
82	  `REGIONAL BY TABLE IN PRIMARY REGION` (the default), so a present-time
83	  read must reach the Ohio leaseholder; every EU `SELECT` hops Frankfurt →
84	  Ohio → back ≈ 105ms. The Frankfurt replica exists for survival, not
85	  reads.
86	
87	These tables live on `globalPool` (`GLOBAL_COCKROACH_DSN`) by design —
88	identity, resources, the cluster registry, and the GitHub-perms mirror
89	tables. Regional pods read them cross-region. PII, audit, and (since
90	COR-378/382) the signing keyset live on the regional pool and are read
91	in-region. See `internal/entirecore/serve_mode_regional.go`.
92	
93	### Background: how CockroachDB avoids the leaseholder hop
94	
95	Every range has one **leaseholder** replica that serves up-to-date reads.
96	In a multi-region database the leaseholder defaults to the primary region,
97	so out-of-region reads pay an RTT to reach it. Three mechanisms remove
98	that hop, with different tradeoffs:
99	
100	| | normal (REGIONAL) read | follower read | `GLOBAL` table | in-process cache |
101	|---|---|---|---|---|
102	| out-of-region read | ~105ms | **~local** | **~local** | **~0 (memory)** |
103	| freshness | up-to-date | stale (~4.8s) | up-to-date | stale (≤ TTL) |
104	| write cost | normal | normal | **higher (commit-wait)** | normal |
105	| where it lives | — | per-query `AS OF SYSTEM TIME` | per-table DDL on the DB | app process |
106	
107	- **Follower reads** exploit the *closed timestamp* so any local replica
108	  can answer a read taken `AS OF SYSTEM TIME follower_read_timestamp()`
109	  (~4.8s stale) without contacting the leaseholder. Read-only; cheap;
110	  works on ordinary tables with no DB change.
111	- **`GLOBAL` tables** use non-blocking transactions so present-time reads
112	  are served fresh from any region's local replica, at the cost of slower
113	  writes everywhere and a multi-region-SQL DDL change to the database.
114	- **In-process caches** keep the value in the pod's memory; ideal for
115	  near-static reference data read far more often than it changes.
116	
117	The decision below picks, per table, the cheapest mechanism that meets
118	that table's freshness need — and deliberately avoids `GLOBAL` (see
119	Alternatives).
120	
121	## Decision
122	
123	Leave the `entirecore` database topology untouched. Assign each hot-path
124	read the locality mechanism that matches its access shape:
125	
126	| read | write rate | freshness need | mechanism | status |
127	|------|-----------|----------------|-----------|--------|
128	| `signing_keys` ×2 | ~never (rotation) | fresh (verification) | **regional pool** (per-jurisdiction keyset) | **shipped** (COR-378/382/415) |
129	| `clusters` | ~never (boot reconcile) | audience-host routing; seconds-stale fine | **in-process TTL cache** | this change |
130	| mirror-URL JOIN | webhook sync | name resolution; seconds-stale OK | **follower read + fresh-on-miss** | shipped in #1795 |
131	| `handles` | rare (identity link) | account→GitHub id; seconds-stale OK | **follower read + fresh-on-miss** | shipped in #1795 |
132	| `github_repos` (`is_private`) | webhook sync | freshness-sensitive | **fresh leaseholder read** | unchanged |
133	| `github_user_repo_access` (authz) | webhook sync | **freshness-critical** (revocation) | **fresh leaseholder read** | unchanged |
134	
135	The load-bearing line is the last one. A follower read there would
136	authorise a just-revoked user for up to the staleness window, and a
137	`GLOBAL` table would tax the frequent perms-sync writes. So the
138	authorisation decision keeps paying the ~105ms fresh read in EU; every
139	read *around* it becomes local or cached. The net EU path goes from a
140	serial chain of Atlantic hops to roughly two fresh authz reads
141	(~210ms) plus local/cached reads.
142	
143	`signing_keys` reaching local latency by **regionalisation** rather than
144	`GLOBAL` is the pivotal choice: it was done for key-isolation and
145	encryption (COR-378/382), and it happens to remove the two signing-key
146	hops for free. With those gone, neither remaining global reference table
147	justifies a `GLOBAL` flip — `clusters` is cheaper to cache, and the perms
148	tables must stay fresh.
149	
150	### Follower reads must fall back to a fresh read on miss
151	
152	A plain follower read breaks **clone-on-create**. `handleCreateMirror`
153	(`core/api/mirrors.go`) commits the `mirror_repos` + `github_mirror_repo_urls`
154	rows and immediately publishes `sync_repo`; the mirror-worker picks that
155	up and token-exchanges within ~100–500ms — well inside the ~4.8s
156	closed-timestamp window. A follower read of `LookupMirrorRefByURL` would
157	return "no mirror at this URL" and the initial clone would 404 (ADR
158	20260521-mirror-bootstrap-on-create). The same applies to a
159	token-exchange immediately after a GitHub link (`handles`).
160	
161	So every follower read on this path is **follower-read-then-fresh-on-error**:
162	serve the local stale read in the common case; on *any* follower error,
163	retry once against the leaseholder. "Any error" (not just `ErrNoRows`) is
164	deliberate — a row newer than the follower timestamp surfaces as
165	`ErrNoRows`, but if the table itself is younger than the staleness window
166	(freshly-migrated test DBs) the follower timestamp predates the table
167	descriptor, so the read returns `undefined_table` (`42P01`) — distinct
168	from a true below-GC-threshold historical-read error — and a single-node
169	cluster that doesn't serve follower reads at all must still resolve. The common path stays local; just-created rows
170	still resolve; the fallback fires only on error so steady-state traffic
171	pays no extra read. A follower failure that isn't an expected miss is
172	logged (and traced via otelpgx) so a silently-degraded follower path is
173	visible.
174	
175	### Read-freshness analysis (stale-present)
176	
177	Reviewed the write/mutation paths to confirm a stale-but-present read
178	can't return a wrong-and-harmful value (COR-371):
179	
180	- **Mirror URL binding is immutable.** `(cluster_slug, url)` is the
181	  primary key and inserts are `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, so a URL can
182	  never be rebound to a different mirror. No stale-present risk.
183	- **Suspend / rename fail closed.** A stale read could miss a <5s-old
184	  `mirror_repos.suspended_at` (reconciler circuit-breaker, ~hourly) or a
185	  `github_repos` owner/repo rename (webhook). Both resolve to a transient
186	  `invalid_target`/`access_denied` that self-heals once the replica
187	  catches up; authz stays keyed on the stable `github_repo_id`. A ~5s lag
188	  is immaterial for both.
189	- **`handles.provider_user_id` is immutable** (part of the PK; only
190	  INSERT/DELETE, never UPDATE). The single stale-present case is a GitHub
191	  **unlink**: a follower read could return the just-removed identity for
192	  ~5s, letting that account mint a mirror token in the window. For a
193	  *private* repo this is gated by the downstream **fresh**
194	  `github_user_repo_access` check. For a *public* repo, `CanPull`
195	  short-circuits on `is_private = false` and never reads the perms table —
196	  so the stale `handles` row is the only identity gate, but a public pull
197	  needs no permission anyway. **Corollary footgun:** this is why
198	  `is_private` stays a fresh read. If `is_private` ever moves to a
199	  follower read, a public→private flip could read stale `is_private =
200	  false`, skip the perms check via the short-circuit, and leak a
201	  now-private repo for ~5s. The deferred `is_private` decision is coupled
202	  to this short-circuit.
203	
204	### Read count vs read locality (why locality, and where count helps)
205	
206	This ADR's first instinct was to make each read *local*; it did not ask
207	whether the path needs all the reads. It does not. The "~7 reads" is a
208	cold/logical count — warm, two are cache-served and one is redundant:
209	
210	| # | read | pool | warm reality |
211	|---|------|------|--------------|
212	| 1 | `refresh_tokens` liveness (COR-309) | regional | local ~4ms; independent of 2–4 → parallelizable |
213	| 2 | `clusters` (host→slug) | global | **cache-served** (this ADR) → ~0 |
214	| 3 | mirror-URL 3-table JOIN | global | the resolve; follower-read (half A) |
215	| 4 | `handles` (account→gh user) | global | independent of 3 → parallelizable; follower-read (half A) |
216	| 5 | `github_repos` (`is_private`) | global | **redundant with #3's row** (see below) |
217	| 6 | `github_user_repo_access` (authz) | global | the decision |
218	| 7 | `signing_keys` (mint) | regional | **cache-served**, regionalised → ~0 |
219	
220	Two structural facts fall out:
221	
222	- **The binding constraint is read #6.** Revocation correctness forbids
223	  caching or follower-reading `github_user_repo_access`, and it lives on
224	  the global pool, so in EU it is an *irreducible* fresh ~105ms
225	  cross-region read. **That ~105ms is the floor** for any design short of
226	  `REGIONAL BY ROW` partitioning the perms tables — neither locality nor
227	  count reduction beats it.
228	- **Read #5 is partly redundant.** `lookupRefByURL` (#3) already JOINs
229	  `github_repos` and returns `github_repo_id`; `CanPull`/`CanPush` then
230	  re-`SELECT`s `github_repos` (`store.go` `lookupRepoVisibility`) only to
231	  get `is_private`. On the **push** path `is_private` is never consulted
232	  (`CanPush` ignores it), so #5 is pure redundant latency there.
233	
234	This is the **user** mirror-exchange path. Platform/automation pulls take
235	a different arm: `peregrine` gets read via the SpiceDB
236	`platform->read_any_repo` pointer (COR-449,
237	`20260616-platform-read-any-repo-pull-arm.md`) set on mirror repos at
238	create time, not via `github_user_repo_access`. So the read-count
239	analysis here scopes the per-user `CanPull`/`CanPush` path; the platform
240	arm is already region-resolved through authz and outside it.
241	
242	Given the #6 floor, **read-count reduction and read-locality are
243	substitutes**, not additive, for the middle reads — both land EU at
244	roughly one fresh authz read plus one other cross-region read (~210ms).
245	The only way to ~105ms is a single fresh JOIN folding #3–#6 into one
246	round trip, which would relocate authorization semantics (the public
247	short-circuit, `ParsePermission`/`Allows`) into a hand-written five-table
248	SQL string spanning three service packages. Not worth it for EU's ~2%,
249	flat traffic; revisit alongside `REGIONAL BY ROW` only if EU grows.
250	
251	There is also a **conflict** between the two levers: #5 exists as a
252	*separate fresh read* precisely so `is_private` stays fresh while the
253	mirror JOIN (#3) is a follower read. Folding `is_private` into a
254	follower #3 would reintroduce the public→private staleness leak
255	(above). So #5 cannot simply be merged into #3 while #3 is a follower
256	read.
257	
258	**What we take now (the free count win):** eliminate #5 on the **push**
259	path. `CanPushToRepo(githubUserID, githubRepoID)` (`core/githubperms`)
260	checks the access edge directly using the `github_repo_id` the ref
261	already carries — no visibility read, no staleness implication (push
262	ignores `is_private`, and #3 already proved existence + non-suspension).
263	The **pull** path keeps #5 as a fresh, separate `is_private` read (the
264	short-circuit gate). Parallelising the independent reads (#1 ‖ #3 ‖ #4)
265	and merging #4 into #6 are larger, fresher alternatives left for a
266	follow-up if EU latency warrants — they tie the follower approach on the
267	EU number, so they are not pursued now.
268	
269	## Mechanism / rollout
270	
271	Three independent, independently-shippable pieces — none touches the
272	database topology:
273	
274	**A. Follower reads — entiredb code (#1795, ships on any cluster).**
275	Annotate `LookupMirrorRefByURL` (`core/mirrorrepo`) and
276	`GitHubUserIDForAccount` (`core/identity`) with
277	`AS OF SYSTEM TIME follower_read_timestamp()` — exact staleness; bounded
278	staleness (`with_max_staleness`) is **not** usable here (the mirror read
279	is a 3-table JOIN and the `handles` read isn't a PK point-lookup, and
280	bounded staleness can't touch more than one row or require an index join)
281	— each wrapped in the fresh-fallback-on-error above. Both are standalone
282	`pool.QueryRow` calls (not inside a read-write txn), so they're
283	follower-eligible as-is, and degrade gracefully to a local read on a
284	single-node dev/CI cluster.
285	
286	**B. `clusters` in-process cache — entiredb code (this change).**
287	`cluster.Store.WithCacheTTL` adds a TTL cache over `GetByPublicHost` and
288	`GetBySlug` (singleflight-guarded, successful loads only — misses and
289	errors are not cached, so a not-yet-reconciled host becomes resolvable as
290	soon as its row appears). Wired with a 5-minute TTL in
291	`internal/entirecore`. The boot-time `cluster.Reconcile` is **unchanged**:
292	the table stays `REGIONAL`, so its per-boot writes remain cheap
293	leaseholder writes with no commit-wait — the contention concern that a
294	`GLOBAL` flip would have introduced does not arise.
295	
296	**C. `signing_keys` regionalisation — already shipped (COR-378/382/415).**
297	`identity/009` dropped the global `signing_keys` table; `regional/010-013`
298	recreated it per-jurisdiction, encrypted; `keyStore` is constructed on the
299	regional pool. No further work here; documented for completeness because
300	it is the largest single contributor to the EU win and supersedes the
301	original "`signing_keys` `GLOBAL`" plan.
302	
303	**Validation.** Confirm in Honeycomb/Datadog that EU `POST /oauth/token`
304	p50 drops toward the ~2-fresh-read floor (~250ms handler) and that EU
305	per-read latency for the cached/follower tables falls to single-digit ms,
306	leaving only `github_repos` + `github_user_repo_access` on the ~105ms
307	global-read path.
308	
309	## Consequences
310	
311	- **EU latency drops to its irreducible floor.** Every read except the
312	  two we intentionally keep fresh becomes local or cached. Projected EU
313	  handler p50 ≈ 2× ~105ms authz reads + local/cached reads ≈ ~250ms, from
314	  ~553ms today (and ~700ms+ before signing-key regionalisation).
315	- **No database change, no `GLOBAL` write tax, no DDL runbook, no
316	  reconcile rework.** The cluster topology and boot path are untouched;
317	  there is no env-divergent schema between dev/CI and prod.
318	- **Clone-on-create preserved.** The follower fresh-fallback-on-miss means
319	  a just-created mirror (or freshly-linked GitHub identity) still
320	  resolves; only that first read pays a second, fresh round trip.
321	- **Bounded staleness windows:** ≤TTL on `clusters` (a near-static
322	  registry; a newly-reconciled host resolves on the next miss), ~5s on the
323	  follower reads (self-healing fail-closed on suspend/rename; ~5s
324	  GitHub-unlink lag gated by the downstream fresh perms check for private
325	  repos).
326	- **US is unaffected** — it already reads in-region leaseholders. This is
327	  purely an EU/out-of-primary-region win, and a narrow one by volume (~2%
328	  of token traffic), realised cheaply because the code is small and the
329	  largest piece (signing-keys) already shipped.
330	
331	## 2026-07-06 addendum: extend the mirror by-id twin to follower reads
332	
333	`core/mirrorrepo.GetRefByID` is the by-id twin of the already-converted
334	`LookupRefByURL`: same `mirror_repos`/`github_repos` data, same
335	`mirror_repos.suspended_at` circuit-breaker, different lookup key
336	(`mirror_repos.id` instead of `(cluster_slug, url)`). It now uses the same
337	follower-read-then-fresh-fallback contract because the staleness exposure is
338	identical: at worst the auth-token-resolution path sees suspension state up to
339	the follower window late (~5s), exactly like the by-URL path, and a
340	just-created placement still resolves via the fresh retry.
341	
342	## Alternatives considered
343	
344	- **`GLOBAL` tables for `clusters` + `signing_keys` (the original plan,
345	  now rejected).** Make the read-mostly reference tables `GLOBAL` so every
346	  region reads them locally *and* fresh. Rejected once signing-keys was
347	  regionalised independently: with the signing-key hops already gone,
348	  `GLOBAL` would only buy the `clusters` read — which an in-process cache
349	  delivers for free and without a write tax. `GLOBAL` also costs:
350	  commit-wait on every write (Standard can't tune `max_offset`); a
351	  per-boot `cluster.Reconcile` that issues unconditional per-row UPDATEs
352	  would pay that cost and contend across concurrently-booting cores during
353	  a fleet deploy; an out-of-band `SET LOCALITY GLOBAL` runbook that can't
354	  be a goose migration (it errors on the single-node dev/CI cluster); and
355	  a silent-revert failure mode (a restore reverts locality with no
356	  signal). All of that to make one near-static read local — not worth it.
357	- **`GLOBAL` for `signing_keys` specifically.** Superseded by
358	  regionalisation (COR-378/382): per-jurisdiction keysets read locally
359	  from the regional pool, with the added benefit of key isolation and
360	  per-region rotation/compromise blast-radius. This is the "regionalise
361	  the keyset" option an earlier draft of this ADR had itself rejected as a
362	  trust-topology change — the team adopted it anyway, for security reasons,
363	  and it resolved the latency as a side effect.
364	- **Parallelise the serial reads in the handler.** Overlapping the
365	  independent reads saves ~100ms today, but once reads are local/cached
366	  the win evaporates — parallelism and locality are substitutes here.
367	  Adding concurrency to a security-critical auth path for a benefit the
368	  locality fix erases is a bad trade.
369	- **Cache everything (incl. perms).** A perms cache would reintroduce the
370	  revocation-staleness hole the fresh authz read exists to close. The
371	  authz read stays fresh by design.
372	- **`REGIONAL BY ROW` for the perms/identity tables.** The scale-out path
373	  *if* EU perms-read latency ever dominates: partition by the cluster's
374	  region so the authz read is in-region too. Not used now — the perms
375	  tables have no natural per-row region affinity, and at ~2% EU volume the
376	  two fresh reads are an acceptable residual. Revisit only if EU volume
377	  grows materially (the 30-day trend is currently flat/noisy, not rising).
378	  The adjacent regional-authz direction for the *list*-shaped authz reads
379	  is COR-319 (`20260612-regional-authz-service-list-queries.md`); a
380	  regional read-only authz surface there could later also serve this
381	  point read in-region without `REGIONAL BY ROW`.
382	
383	## Out of scope / open questions
384	
385	- **`github_repos.is_private` freshness classification.** Could in
386	  principle join the follower-read set, but only after a focused review of
387	  the `CanPull`/`CanPush` short-circuit (see the footgun above). Stays a
388	  fresh read until that review lands.
389	- **Other `globalPool` reads outside the token-exchange hot path.** This
390	  ADR scopes the `/oauth/token` reads; the same mechanisms likely help
391	  elsewhere but should be validated per-path before broadening.
392	- **Follower-fallback observability.** The fallback logs a filtered WARN;
393	  a fallback-rate counter/SLO is the recommended ongoing guard against a
394	  silently-degraded follower path (every read paying attempt + fresh).
395	
396	## Follow-up: mirror-create path (COR-371 extension)
397	
398	`POST /api/v1/mirrors` (`CreateMirrorPlacement`) is the second EU-slow
399	global-read chain. The same per-read triage applies, but the create path
400	has a wrinkle the token-exchange path doesn't: `EnsureRepoKnown` upserts
401	the `github_installations` + `github_repos` rows for the target repo *in
402	the same request*, just before the reads that consume them. A follower
403	read (~4.8s stale) cannot see a <1s-old write, so the mechanism only helps
404	for a read whose row was last written **outside** this request's ~4.8s
405	window (a prior MVCC version exists).
406	
407	| create-path read | table | last written | decision |
408	|------|------|------|----------|
409	| `GitHubHandleForAccount` (`requireGitHubUser`) | `handles` | GitHub-link time (long prior) | **follower + fresh-fallback** |
410	| `LookupInstallationByLogin` (authorize) | `github_installations` | App install (usually long prior; re-upserted this request but the old version is correct — id/type/login are stable) | **follower + fresh-fallback** |
411	| `LookupInstallationIDForRepo` (finish, 412 gate) | `github_repos` | **this request** (`EnsureRepoKnown`) | **stays fresh** — a stale NULL/superseded value spuriously 412s or stamps the wrong installation onto the data-plane row |
412	| `IsRepoPrivate` (visibility seed) | `github_repos` | **this request** (`EnsureRepoKnown`) | **read eliminated** — `EnsureRepoKnown` now returns the visibility off the GitHub object it just persisted, so the seed needs no DB read at all (a read of your own seconds-old write could never be follower-served). The shared `IsRepoPrivate` method stays fresh for its remaining caller, the pull gate's public short-circuit (the footgun above) |
413	| `findGitHubLinkedOrg` (authorize, org-owned) | `orgs ⋈ github_org_links` | first mirror of the org (long prior) | **follower + fresh-fallback** — fallback also covers the race-loser re-read in `CreateOrFindGitHubLinkedOrg` |
414	| `findProjectByExactName` (`CreateOrFindMirrorsProject`) | `projects` | owner's first mirror on the cluster (long prior) | **follower + fresh-fallback** — the fallback-on-not-found is load-bearing: without it a stale miss on a seconds-old project would detour through the create branch's unique-violation handling |
415	
416	The linked-org find also carried an **unconditional write**: a login-refresh
417	`UPDATE github_org_links` on every find, a cross-region round trip to refresh
418	a denormalized login that almost never changes. The stored login now rides
419	the find SELECT and the UPDATE is issued only on drift (a GitHub org rename),
420	so the steady-state find is read-only.
421	
422	There is **no** synchronous `mirror_repos` dupe-check or
423	`github_user_repo_access` read on this path to convert: `mirrorrepo.Create`
424	is idempotent via `ON CONFLICT` inside its own read-write txn (not
425	follower-eligible), and the collaborator read-model is touched only by the
426	**async** `perms_backfill` job (`enqueueMirrorPermsBackfill`), off the
427	request path. So the create-path win is the two reads above; the writes
428	(`repo_registry`, `github_repos`/`github_installations` upserts, the
429	mirror + URL rows, the SpiceDB grants) keep paying the cross-region write
430	floor, as intended.
431	
432	The SpiceDB **write count** on the path was also trimmed (adjacent to, not
433	part of, the read-locality mechanism): the find paths of
434	`CreateOrFindGitHubLinkedOrg` and `CreateOrFindMirrorsProject` used to
435	re-assert their system tuples (`PlatformOrgCreated` / `ProjectCreated`) as
436	standalone self-heal writes on **every** create — two sequential round
437	trips to the primary-region authz-writer. Those tuples now ride
438	`RegisterMirrorAsNativeRepo`'s single batched `WriteRelationships`
439	(`authz.MirrorPlacementRegistered`), which every create ends in, preserving
440	the orphan self-heal at zero extra round trips.

# entire-core read locality in the multi-region global CockroachDB

Status: Accepted

Tracking: [COR-371](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/COR-371)

## TLDR

`POST /oauth/token` in EU is far slower than US (EU p50 ~553ms in the
handler / ~789ms end-to-end vs US ~30ms) because the token-exchange path
issues a handful of CockroachDB reads strictly in series, and each read
against the **global** pool is a cross-Atlantic round trip from the
Frankfurt pod to the range leaseholder in Ohio (the global cluster's
primary region). Measured directly: an EU read of the global cluster is
~105ms; an EU read of the regional EU cluster is ~4ms.

The fix is read locality, achieved **without `GLOBAL` tables**:

- **`signing_keys` — regionalised** (already shipped, COR-378/382/415).
  Each jurisdiction mints and serves its own keys from its regional pool,
  so the two per-request signing-key reads are now ~4ms local reads
  instead of cross-Atlantic hops. This is the single biggest realised win
  and the reason an earlier "make `signing_keys` `GLOBAL`" plan was
  dropped.
- **`clusters` — in-process cached.** The cluster registry is near-static
  fixture data; an in-process TTL cache (`cluster.Store.WithCacheTTL`,
  mirroring the existing signing-key cache) removes the read from the hot
  path after the first lookup. No table-locality change.
- **mirror-URL resolution and GitHub-identity mapping — follower reads**
  with **fresh-fallback-on-error**, so the staleness-tolerant per-request
  lookups read from the local replica (~4ms) while clone-on-create still
  works.
- **The authorisation decision (`github_user_repo_access`, and the
  `github_repos.is_private` flag it depends on) stays a fresh
  leaseholder read** — revocation correctness forbids staleness. This is
  the irreducible residual: ~2 cross-region reads (~210ms) on a pull in
  EU; a push drops the redundant visibility read, leaving ~1 (~105ms).

No `GLOBAL` table, no multi-region-SQL DDL runbook, no reconcile rework.
The CockroachDB `entirecore` database is left exactly as it is.

## Context

Investigation on 2026-05-29 (Honeycomb `entire.io` / `entire-core`),
re-confirmed 2026-06-16. `POST /oauth/token` latency by region:

| region | p50 (May baseline) | p50 (2026-06-16, 7d) | p95 | p99 |
|--------|------|------|-----|-----|
| us-east-2 (primary) | 199ms | **25ms** (e2e) / 30ms (handler) | 56ms | 88ms |
| eu-central-1 | 1030ms | **789ms** (e2e) / 553ms (handler) | 1181ms | 1219ms |

EU is ~2% of token volume (~947 handler calls / 7d) but owns essentially
the entire latency tail. A representative EU trace is a series of `client`
DB spans running back-to-back with near-zero overlap, each a clean
multiple of the ~100ms Frankfurt↔Ohio RTT.

**The mechanism, measured directly.** Splitting EU (`eu-central-1`) DB
reads by the database host they hit (7d):

| EU read target | p50 | p99 | reads/7d |
|----------------|-----|-----|----------|
| `entire-core-prod-global` (Ohio leaseholder) | **104.8ms** | 310ms | 1,559 |
| `entire-core-prod-eu` (regional, in-region) | **4.0ms** | 25ms | 703 |

This is the whole problem in two rows: reads on the **global** pool cost
a ~105ms Atlantic hop from EU; reads on the **regional** pool are local.
It also confirms the signing-key regionalisation landed — those reads are
now in the 4ms bucket, off the hot path. What remains slow in EU is the
set of reads still on the global pool: `clusters`, the
`github_mirror_repo_urls → mirror_repos → github_repos` JOIN, `handles`,
`github_repos` (`is_private`), and `github_user_repo_access`.

The global cluster is `entire-core-prod-global` (CockroachDB v25.4.10,
Cloud **Standard**, AWS, multi-region: Frankfurt `eu-central-1`, Ohio
`us-east-2` **PRIMARY**, Oregon `us-west-2`). Two facts pin the cause:

- **The EU pod's SQL gateway is local.** A `BEGIN` (which touches no
  leaseholder) from `entire-core-regional-eu` against the global cluster
  is ~1.7ms — the region-less DSN host geo-routes EU pods to a Frankfurt
  gateway. The connection is *not* crossing the Atlantic.
- **The leaseholders are in Ohio.** The global tables are
  `REGIONAL BY TABLE IN PRIMARY REGION` (the default), so a present-time
  read must reach the Ohio leaseholder; every EU `SELECT` hops Frankfurt →
  Ohio → back ≈ 105ms. The Frankfurt replica exists for survival, not
  reads.

These tables live on `globalPool` (`GLOBAL_COCKROACH_DSN`) by design —
identity, resources, the cluster registry, and the GitHub-perms mirror
tables. Regional pods read them cross-region. PII, audit, and (since
COR-378/382) the signing keyset live on the regional pool and are read
in-region. See `internal/entirecore/serve_mode_regional.go`.

### Background: how CockroachDB avoids the leaseholder hop

Every range has one **leaseholder** replica that serves up-to-date reads.
In a multi-region database the leaseholder defaults to the primary region,
so out-of-region reads pay an RTT to reach it. Three mechanisms remove
that hop, with different tradeoffs:

| | normal (REGIONAL) read | follower read | `GLOBAL` table | in-process cache |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| out-of-region read | ~105ms | **~local** | **~local** | **~0 (memory)** |
| freshness | up-to-date | stale (~4.8s) | up-to-date | stale (≤ TTL) |
| write cost | normal | normal | **higher (commit-wait)** | normal |
| where it lives | — | per-query `AS OF SYSTEM TIME` | per-table DDL on the DB | app process |

- **Follower reads** exploit the *closed timestamp* so any local replica
  can answer a read taken `AS OF SYSTEM TIME follower_read_timestamp()`
  (~4.8s stale) without contacting the leaseholder. Read-only; cheap;
  works on ordinary tables with no DB change.
- **`GLOBAL` tables** use non-blocking transactions so present-time reads
  are served fresh from any region's local replica, at the cost of slower
  writes everywhere and a multi-region-SQL DDL change to the database.
- **In-process caches** keep the value in the pod's memory; ideal for
  near-static reference data read far more often than it changes.

The decision below picks, per table, the cheapest mechanism that meets
that table's freshness need — and deliberately avoids `GLOBAL` (see
Alternatives).

## Decision

Leave the `entirecore` database topology untouched. Assign each hot-path
read the locality mechanism that matches its access shape:

| read | write rate | freshness need | mechanism | status |
|------|-----------|----------------|-----------|--------|
| `signing_keys` ×2 | ~never (rotation) | fresh (verification) | **regional pool** (per-jurisdiction keyset) | **shipped** (COR-378/382/415) |
| `clusters` | ~never (boot reconcile) | audience-host routing; seconds-stale fine | **in-process TTL cache** | this change |
| mirror-URL JOIN | webhook sync | name resolution; seconds-stale OK | **follower read + fresh-on-miss** | shipped in #1795 |
| `handles` | rare (identity link) | account→GitHub id; seconds-stale OK | **follower read + fresh-on-miss** | shipped in #1795 |
| `github_repos` (`is_private`) | webhook sync | freshness-sensitive | **fresh leaseholder read** | unchanged |
| `github_user_repo_access` (authz) | webhook sync | **freshness-critical** (revocation) | **fresh leaseholder read** | unchanged |

The load-bearing line is the last one. A follower read there would
authorise a just-revoked user for up to the staleness window, and a
`GLOBAL` table would tax the frequent perms-sync writes. So the
authorisation decision keeps paying the ~105ms fresh read in EU; every
read *around* it becomes local or cached. The net EU path goes from a
serial chain of Atlantic hops to roughly two fresh authz reads
(~210ms) plus local/cached reads.

`signing_keys` reaching local latency by **regionalisation** rather than
`GLOBAL` is the pivotal choice: it was done for key-isolation and
encryption (COR-378/382), and it happens to remove the two signing-key
hops for free. With those gone, neither remaining global reference table
justifies a `GLOBAL` flip — `clusters` is cheaper to cache, and the perms
tables must stay fresh.

### Follower reads must fall back to a fresh read on miss

A plain follower read breaks **clone-on-create**. `handleCreateMirror`
(`core/api/mirrors.go`) commits the `mirror_repos` + `github_mirror_repo_urls`
rows and immediately publishes `sync_repo`; the mirror-worker picks that
up and token-exchanges within ~100–500ms — well inside the ~4.8s
closed-timestamp window. A follower read of `LookupMirrorRefByURL` would
return "no mirror at this URL" and the initial clone would 404 (ADR
20260521-mirror-bootstrap-on-create). The same applies to a
token-exchange immediately after a GitHub link (`handles`).

So every follower read on this path is **follower-read-then-fresh-on-error**:
serve the local stale read in the common case; on *any* follower error,
retry once against the leaseholder. "Any error" (not just `ErrNoRows`) is
deliberate — a row newer than the follower timestamp surfaces as
`ErrNoRows`, but if the table itself is younger than the staleness window
(freshly-migrated test DBs) the follower timestamp predates the table
descriptor, so the read returns `undefined_table` (`42P01`) — distinct
from a true below-GC-threshold historical-read error — and a single-node
cluster that doesn't serve follower reads at all must still resolve. The common path stays local; just-created rows
still resolve; the fallback fires only on error so steady-state traffic
pays no extra read. A follower failure that isn't an expected miss is
logged (and traced via otelpgx) so a silently-degraded follower path is
visible.

### Read-freshness analysis (stale-present)

Reviewed the write/mutation paths to confirm a stale-but-present read
can't return a wrong-and-harmful value (COR-371):

- **Mirror URL binding is immutable.** `(cluster_slug, url)` is the
  primary key and inserts are `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, so a URL can
  never be rebound to a different mirror. No stale-present risk.
- **Suspend / rename fail closed.** A stale read could miss a <5s-old
  `mirror_repos.suspended_at` (reconciler circuit-breaker, ~hourly) or a
  `github_repos` owner/repo rename (webhook). Both resolve to a transient
  `invalid_target`/`access_denied` that self-heals once the replica
  catches up; authz stays keyed on the stable `github_repo_id`. A ~5s lag
  is immaterial for both.
- **`handles.provider_user_id` is immutable** (part of the PK; only
  INSERT/DELETE, never UPDATE). The single stale-present case is a GitHub
  **unlink**: a follower read could return the just-removed identity for
  ~5s, letting that account mint a mirror token in the window. For a
  *private* repo this is gated by the downstream **fresh**
  `github_user_repo_access` check. For a *public* repo, `CanPull`
  short-circuits on `is_private = false` and never reads the perms table —
  so the stale `handles` row is the only identity gate, but a public pull
  needs no permission anyway. **Corollary footgun:** this is why
  `is_private` stays a fresh read. If `is_private` ever moves to a
  follower read, a public→private flip could read stale `is_private =
  false`, skip the perms check via the short-circuit, and leak a
  now-private repo for ~5s. The deferred `is_private` decision is coupled
  to this short-circuit.

### Read count vs read locality (why locality, and where count helps)

This ADR's first instinct was to make each read *local*; it did not ask
whether the path needs all the reads. It does not. The "~7 reads" is a
cold/logical count — warm, two are cache-served and one is redundant:

| # | read | pool | warm reality |
|---|------|------|--------------|
| 1 | `refresh_tokens` liveness (COR-309) | regional | local ~4ms; independent of 2–4 → parallelizable |
| 2 | `clusters` (host→slug) | global | **cache-served** (this ADR) → ~0 |
| 3 | mirror-URL 3-table JOIN | global | the resolve; follower-read (half A) |
| 4 | `handles` (account→gh user) | global | independent of 3 → parallelizable; follower-read (half A) |
| 5 | `github_repos` (`is_private`) | global | **redundant with #3's row** (see below) |
| 6 | `github_user_repo_access` (authz) | global | the decision |
| 7 | `signing_keys` (mint) | regional | **cache-served**, regionalised → ~0 |

Two structural facts fall out:

- **The binding constraint is read #6.** Revocation correctness forbids
  caching or follower-reading `github_user_repo_access`, and it lives on
  the global pool, so in EU it is an *irreducible* fresh ~105ms
  cross-region read. **That ~105ms is the floor** for any design short of
  `REGIONAL BY ROW` partitioning the perms tables — neither locality nor
  count reduction beats it.
- **Read #5 is partly redundant.** `lookupRefByURL` (#3) already JOINs
  `github_repos` and returns `github_repo_id`; `CanPull`/`CanPush` then
  re-`SELECT`s `github_repos` (`store.go` `lookupRepoVisibility`) only to
  get `is_private`. On the **push** path `is_private` is never consulted
  (`CanPush` ignores it), so #5 is pure redundant latency there.

This is the **user** mirror-exchange path. Platform/automation pulls take
a different arm: `peregrine` gets read via the SpiceDB
`platform->read_any_repo` pointer (COR-449,
`20260616-platform-read-any-repo-pull-arm.md`) set on mirror repos at
create time, not via `github_user_repo_access`. So the read-count
analysis here scopes the per-user `CanPull`/`CanPush` path; the platform
arm is already region-resolved through authz and outside it.

Given the #6 floor, **read-count reduction and read-locality are
substitutes**, not additive, for the middle reads — both land EU at
roughly one fresh authz read plus one other cross-region read (~210ms).
The only way to ~105ms is a single fresh JOIN folding #3–#6 into one
round trip, which would relocate authorization semantics (the public
short-circuit, `ParsePermission`/`Allows`) into a hand-written five-table
SQL string spanning three service packages. Not worth it for EU's ~2%,
flat traffic; revisit alongside `REGIONAL BY ROW` only if EU grows.

There is also a **conflict** between the two levers: #5 exists as a
*separate fresh read* precisely so `is_private` stays fresh while the
mirror JOIN (#3) is a follower read. Folding `is_private` into a
follower #3 would reintroduce the public→private staleness leak
(above). So #5 cannot simply be merged into #3 while #3 is a follower
read.

**What we take now (the free count win):** eliminate #5 on the **push**
path. `CanPushToRepo(githubUserID, githubRepoID)` (`core/githubperms`)
checks the access edge directly using the `github_repo_id` the ref
already carries — no visibility read, no staleness implication (push
ignores `is_private`, and #3 already proved existence + non-suspension).
The **pull** path keeps #5 as a fresh, separate `is_private` read (the
short-circuit gate). Parallelising the independent reads (#1 ‖ #3 ‖ #4)
and merging #4 into #6 are larger, fresher alternatives left for a
follow-up if EU latency warrants — they tie the follower approach on the
EU number, so they are not pursued now.

## Mechanism / rollout

Three independent, independently-shippable pieces — none touches the
database topology:

**A. Follower reads — entiredb code (#1795, ships on any cluster).**
Annotate `LookupMirrorRefByURL` (`core/mirrorrepo`) and
`GitHubUserIDForAccount` (`core/identity`) with
`AS OF SYSTEM TIME follower_read_timestamp()` — exact staleness; bounded
staleness (`with_max_staleness`) is **not** usable here (the mirror read
is a 3-table JOIN and the `handles` read isn't a PK point-lookup, and
bounded staleness can't touch more than one row or require an index join)
— each wrapped in the fresh-fallback-on-error above. Both are standalone
`pool.QueryRow` calls (not inside a read-write txn), so they're
follower-eligible as-is, and degrade gracefully to a local read on a
single-node dev/CI cluster.

**B. `clusters` in-process cache — entiredb code (this change).**
`cluster.Store.WithCacheTTL` adds a TTL cache over `GetByPublicHost` and
`GetBySlug` (singleflight-guarded, successful loads only — misses and
errors are not cached, so a not-yet-reconciled host becomes resolvable as
soon as its row appears). Wired with a 5-minute TTL in
`internal/entirecore`. The boot-time `cluster.Reconcile` is **unchanged**:
the table stays `REGIONAL`, so its per-boot writes remain cheap
leaseholder writes with no commit-wait — the contention concern that a
`GLOBAL` flip would have introduced does not arise.

**C. `signing_keys` regionalisation — already shipped (COR-378/382/415).**
`identity/009` dropped the global `signing_keys` table; `regional/010-013`
recreated it per-jurisdiction, encrypted; `keyStore` is constructed on the
regional pool. No further work here; documented for completeness because
it is the largest single contributor to the EU win and supersedes the
original "`signing_keys` `GLOBAL`" plan.

**Validation.** Confirm in Honeycomb/Datadog that EU `POST /oauth/token`
p50 drops toward the ~2-fresh-read floor (~250ms handler) and that EU
per-read latency for the cached/follower tables falls to single-digit ms,
leaving only `github_repos` + `github_user_repo_access` on the ~105ms
global-read path.

## Consequences

- **EU latency drops to its irreducible floor.** Every read except the
  two we intentionally keep fresh becomes local or cached. Projected EU
  handler p50 ≈ 2× ~105ms authz reads + local/cached reads ≈ ~250ms, from
  ~553ms today (and ~700ms+ before signing-key regionalisation).
- **No database change, no `GLOBAL` write tax, no DDL runbook, no
  reconcile rework.** The cluster topology and boot path are untouched;
  there is no env-divergent schema between dev/CI and prod.
- **Clone-on-create preserved.** The follower fresh-fallback-on-miss means
  a just-created mirror (or freshly-linked GitHub identity) still
  resolves; only that first read pays a second, fresh round trip.
- **Bounded staleness windows:** ≤TTL on `clusters` (a near-static
  registry; a newly-reconciled host resolves on the next miss), ~5s on the
  follower reads (self-healing fail-closed on suspend/rename; ~5s
  GitHub-unlink lag gated by the downstream fresh perms check for private
  repos).
- **US is unaffected** — it already reads in-region leaseholders. This is
  purely an EU/out-of-primary-region win, and a narrow one by volume (~2%
  of token traffic), realised cheaply because the code is small and the
  largest piece (signing-keys) already shipped.

## 2026-07-06 addendum: extend the mirror by-id twin to follower reads

`core/mirrorrepo.GetRefByID` is the by-id twin of the already-converted
`LookupRefByURL`: same `mirror_repos`/`github_repos` data, same
`mirror_repos.suspended_at` circuit-breaker, different lookup key
(`mirror_repos.id` instead of `(cluster_slug, url)`). It now uses the same
follower-read-then-fresh-fallback contract because the staleness exposure is
identical: at worst the auth-token-resolution path sees suspension state up to
the follower window late (~5s), exactly like the by-URL path, and a
just-created placement still resolves via the fresh retry.

## Alternatives considered

- **`GLOBAL` tables for `clusters` + `signing_keys` (the original plan,
  now rejected).** Make the read-mostly reference tables `GLOBAL` so every
  region reads them locally *and* fresh. Rejected once signing-keys was
  regionalised independently: with the signing-key hops already gone,
  `GLOBAL` would only buy the `clusters` read — which an in-process cache
  delivers for free and without a write tax. `GLOBAL` also costs:
  commit-wait on every write (Standard can't tune `max_offset`); a
  per-boot `cluster.Reconcile` that issues unconditional per-row UPDATEs
  would pay that cost and contend across concurrently-booting cores during
  a fleet deploy; an out-of-band `SET LOCALITY GLOBAL` runbook that can't
  be a goose migration (it errors on the single-node dev/CI cluster); and
  a silent-revert failure mode (a restore reverts locality with no
  signal). All of that to make one near-static read local — not worth it.
- **`GLOBAL` for `signing_keys` specifically.** Superseded by
  regionalisation (COR-378/382): per-jurisdiction keysets read locally
  from the regional pool, with the added benefit of key isolation and
  per-region rotation/compromise blast-radius. This is the "regionalise
  the keyset" option an earlier draft of this ADR had itself rejected as a
  trust-topology change — the team adopted it anyway, for security reasons,
  and it resolved the latency as a side effect.
- **Parallelise the serial reads in the handler.** Overlapping the
  independent reads saves ~100ms today, but once reads are local/cached
  the win evaporates — parallelism and locality are substitutes here.
  Adding concurrency to a security-critical auth path for a benefit the
  locality fix erases is a bad trade.
- **Cache everything (incl. perms).** A perms cache would reintroduce the
  revocation-staleness hole the fresh authz read exists to close. The
  authz read stays fresh by design.
- **`REGIONAL BY ROW` for the perms/identity tables.** The scale-out path
  *if* EU perms-read latency ever dominates: partition by the cluster's
  region so the authz read is in-region too. Not used now — the perms
  tables have no natural per-row region affinity, and at ~2% EU volume the
  two fresh reads are an acceptable residual. Revisit only if EU volume
  grows materially (the 30-day trend is currently flat/noisy, not rising).
  The adjacent regional-authz direction for the *list*-shaped authz reads
  is COR-319 (`20260612-regional-authz-service-list-queries.md`); a
  regional read-only authz surface there could later also serve this
  point read in-region without `REGIONAL BY ROW`.

## Out of scope / open questions

- **`github_repos.is_private` freshness classification.** Could in
  principle join the follower-read set, but only after a focused review of
  the `CanPull`/`CanPush` short-circuit (see the footgun above). Stays a
  fresh read until that review lands.
- **Other `globalPool` reads outside the token-exchange hot path.** This
  ADR scopes the `/oauth/token` reads; the same mechanisms likely help
  elsewhere but should be validated per-path before broadening.
- **Follower-fallback observability.** The fallback logs a filtered WARN;
  a fallback-rate counter/SLO is the recommended ongoing guard against a
  silently-degraded follower path (every read paying attempt + fresh).

## Follow-up: mirror-create path (COR-371 extension)

`POST /api/v1/mirrors` (`CreateMirrorPlacement`) is the second EU-slow
global-read chain. The same per-read triage applies, but the create path
has a wrinkle the token-exchange path doesn't: `EnsureRepoKnown` upserts
the `github_installations` + `github_repos` rows for the target repo *in
the same request*, just before the reads that consume them. A follower
read (~4.8s stale) cannot see a <1s-old write, so the mechanism only helps
for a read whose row was last written **outside** this request's ~4.8s
window (a prior MVCC version exists).

| create-path read | table | last written | decision |
|------|------|------|----------|
| `GitHubHandleForAccount` (`requireGitHubUser`) | `handles` | GitHub-link time (long prior) | **follower + fresh-fallback** |
| `LookupInstallationByLogin` (authorize) | `github_installations` | App install (usually long prior; re-upserted this request but the old version is correct — id/type/login are stable) | **follower + fresh-fallback** |
| `LookupInstallationIDForRepo` (finish, 412 gate) | `github_repos` | **this request** (`EnsureRepoKnown`) | **stays fresh** — a stale NULL/superseded value spuriously 412s or stamps the wrong installation onto the data-plane row |
| `IsRepoPrivate` (visibility seed) | `github_repos` | **this request** (`EnsureRepoKnown`) | **read eliminated** — `EnsureRepoKnown` now returns the visibility off the GitHub object it just persisted, so the seed needs no DB read at all (a read of your own seconds-old write could never be follower-served). The shared `IsRepoPrivate` method stays fresh for its remaining caller, the pull gate's public short-circuit (the footgun above) |
| `findGitHubLinkedOrg` (authorize, org-owned) | `orgs ⋈ github_org_links` | first mirror of the org (long prior) | **follower + fresh-fallback** — fallback also covers the race-loser re-read in `CreateOrFindGitHubLinkedOrg` |
| `findProjectByExactName` (`CreateOrFindMirrorsProject`) | `projects` | owner's first mirror on the cluster (long prior) | **follower + fresh-fallback** — the fallback-on-not-found is load-bearing: without it a stale miss on a seconds-old project would detour through the create branch's unique-violation handling |

The linked-org find also carried an **unconditional write**: a login-refresh
`UPDATE github_org_links` on every find, a cross-region round trip to refresh
a denormalized login that almost never changes. The stored login now rides
the find SELECT and the UPDATE is issued only on drift (a GitHub org rename),
so the steady-state find is read-only.

There is **no** synchronous `mirror_repos` dupe-check or
`github_user_repo_access` read on this path to convert: `mirrorrepo.Create`
is idempotent via `ON CONFLICT` inside its own read-write txn (not
follower-eligible), and the collaborator read-model is touched only by the
**async** `perms_backfill` job (`enqueueMirrorPermsBackfill`), off the
request path. So the create-path win is the two reads above; the writes
(`repo_registry`, `github_repos`/`github_installations` upserts, the
mirror + URL rows, the SpiceDB grants) keep paying the cross-region write
floor, as intended.

The SpiceDB **write count** on the path was also trimmed (adjacent to, not
part of, the read-locality mechanism): the find paths of
`CreateOrFindGitHubLinkedOrg` and `CreateOrFindMirrorsProject` used to
re-assert their system tuples (`PlatformOrgCreated` / `ProjectCreated`) as
standalone self-heal writes on **every** create — two sequential round
trips to the primary-region authz-writer. Those tuples now ride
`RegisterMirrorAsNativeRepo`'s single batched `WriteRelationships`
(`authz.MirrorPlacementRegistered`), which every create ends in, preserving
the orphan self-heal at zero extra round trips.

524			case errors.Is(err, errTrustReconcilerDisabled):
525				// Seed provider not configured: leave rootSeedProvider nil, which
526				// disables the publish path (buildTrustReconciler idles below).
527			case err != nil:
528				cleanup()
529				return deps, func() {}, fmt.Errorf("trust reconciler: root seed provider: %w", err)
530			default:
531				deps.rootSeedProvider = seeds
532			}
533	
534			tlsTransport, err := newInternalTLSTransport(cfg)
535			if err != nil {
536				cleanup()
537				return deps, func() {}, fmt.Errorf("trust reconciler: internal TLS transport: %w", err)
538			}
539			bridge, err := buildRepoBridge(ctx, cfg, tlsTransport, deps.clusterStore)
540			if err != nil {
541				cleanup()
542				return deps, func() {}, fmt.Errorf("trust reconciler: build entiredb bridge: %w", err)
543			}
544			// The accept phase does not depend on the root seed: it only verifies
545			// what an owning core in any jurisdiction staged.
546			worker, err := buildPlacementAcceptanceWorker(cfg, deps, bridge)
547			switch {
548			case errors.Is(err, errTrustReconcilerDisabled):
549			case err != nil:
550				cleanup()
551				return deps, func() {}, err
552			default:
553				deps.placementAcceptanceWorker = worker
554			}
555	
556			rec, err := buildTrustReconciler(cfg, deps, bridge)
557			switch {
558			case errors.Is(err, errTrustReconcilerDisabled):
559				// Not provisioned yet (no seed / unpublishable bridge / no fixture root
560				// profile): omit the subsystem. The admin surface still records intents
561				// and reports "not provisioned".
562			case err != nil:
563				cleanup()
564				return deps, func() {}, err
565			default:
566				deps.trustReconciler = rec
567				sweep, err := buildRootOnCreateSweep(cfg, deps)
568				if err != nil {
569					cleanup()
570					return deps, func() {}, err
571				}
572				deps.trustRootOnCreateSweep = sweep
573			}
574		}
575	
576		// Mirror-URL data-plane drainer (COR-1221): applies the URL moves the
577		// alias reconcile owes to this jurisdiction's clusters. Builds its own
578		// bridge like the executor above. A core with no usable bridge (no
579		// internal client cert, no clusters) logs and runs without it — the owed
580		// rows wait in the outbox rather than failing boot.
581		if cfg.MirrorURLDataplaneDrainerEnabled {
582			deps.mirrorURLDrainer = buildMirrorURLDrainer(ctx, cfg, deps)
583		}
584	
585		// Cell-cleanup drainer (COR-1820): tears down the cell resources a
586		// terminally failed provisioning left allocated. Unflagged — the queue is
587		// the only owner of that state once the control plane gives up on the
588		// repo. A core with no usable bridge logs and runs without it; the owed
589		// rows wait rather than failing boot.
590		deps.repoCellCleanupDrainer = buildRepoCellCleanupDrainer(ctx, cfg, deps)
591	
592		signingKeyCipher, err := buildSigningKeyCipher(ctx, cfg)
593		if err != nil {
594			cleanup()
595			return deps, func() {}, fmt.Errorf("signing key cipher: %w", err)
596		}
597		// Signing keys live in the region's own DB (regionalPool), never global.
598		// EnsureSigningKey loads this region's key or mints one if absent. Per-region
599		// kids are fine: cross-region verification fetches each region's JWKS.
600		deps.keyStore = authn.NewKeyStore(regionalPool, signingKeyCipher, authn.WithCacheTTL(signingKeyCacheTTL))
601		if _, err := deps.keyStore.EnsureSigningKey(ctx); err != nil {
602			cleanup()
603			return deps, func() {}, fmt.Errorf("ensure signing key: %w", err)
604		}
605		// RS256 is never the signing algorithm (EdDSA is), but OIDC Core mandates
606		// RS256 support, so persist an RSA key for discovery + JWKS (COR-415).
607		if _, err := deps.keyStore.EnsureRSAKey(ctx); err != nil {
608			cleanup()
609			return deps, func() {}, fmt.Errorf("ensure rsa signing key: %w", err)
610		}
611		// Keep the signing-key + JWKS cache warm off the request path (COR-846):
612		// low-traffic EU/AU pods mint too rarely to keep a TTL-only cache from
613		// expiring, so every request paid the KMS decrypt. The loop stops when ctx
614		// (the serve-lifetime context) is cancelled.
615		deps.keyStore.StartBackgroundRefresh(ctx)
616		// iss=aud=cfg.IssuerClaim(). The URL form lets external verifiers
617		// derive JWKS from iss (RFC 8414); in this repo verifiers are still
618		// configured with explicit JWKS URLs, but the iss must be URL-shaped
619		// for callers like the partial.to data plane that do that lookup.
620		iss := cfg.IssuerClaim()
621		deps.jwtIssuer = authn.NewJWTIssuer(deps.keyStore, authn.LoginTokenTTL, iss, iss)
622	
623		// Regional serves its own JWKS on the public listener (localhost) — no
624		// amplification risk, so disable the unknown-kid refetch throttle and
625		// pick up our own rotated kid at once. Every bearer token on this pod
626		// passes through here, so the keeper never idles out.
627		deps.verifier = jwtverify.New(cfg.LocalJWKSURL(), 5*time.Minute,
628			jwtverify.WithAudiences([]string{cfg.AuthBaseURL}),
629			jwtverify.WithObserver(authn.RecordTokenVerifiedObserver("core")),
630			jwtverify.WithMinRefetchInterval(0),
631			jwtverify.WithPersistentKeeper(),
632		)
633	
634		deps.oauthStateStore = authn.NewOAuthStateStore(regionalPool)
635	
636		// Empty cipher disables the github-tokens path entirely
637		// (link/STS routes 503), which is the safe default for a fresh
638		// regional cluster before KMS provisioning lands.
639		if cfg.GitHubTokenCipher != "" {
640			ghCipher, err := buildGitHubTokenCipher(ctx, cfg)
641			if err != nil {
642				cleanup()
643				return deps, func() {}, fmt.Errorf("github token cipher: %w", err)
644			}
645			// github_user_tokens lives in the GLOBAL tier (COR-932) so a user's
646			// GitHub link is readable/writable at every cell, not just the one that
647			// seeded it. The cipher key is a multi-region KMS key so any cell can
648			// decrypt the shared ciphertext.
649			deps.githubTokens = githubtokens.NewService(globalPool, ghCipher, cfg.GitHubClientID, cfg.GitHubClientSecret)
650	
651			// Same cipher config protects the COR-596 installation-token cache.
652			instCipher, err := buildInstallationTokenCipher(ctx, cfg)
653			if err != nil {
654				cleanup()
655				return deps, func() {}, fmt.Errorf("installation token cipher: %w", err)
656			}
657			deps.installationTokenStore = githubinsttoken.NewStore(regionalPool, instCipher)
658		}
659	
660		deps.regionHosts = cfg.ParseRegionHosts()
661		authHostsRaw := cfg.ParseJurisdictionAuthHosts()
662		deps.jurisdictionAuthHosts = MergeAuthHosts(authHostsRaw, deps.regionHosts)
663		if err := errOnPartialJurisdictionAuthHosts(authHostsRaw, deps.regionHosts); err != nil {
664			cleanup()
665			return deps, func() {}, err
666		}
667		if cfg.HomeRegionCookieSecret != "" {
668			deps.cookie = authn.NewHomeJurisdictionCookie([]byte(cfg.HomeRegionCookieSecret), cfg.CookieDomain)
669			deps.commitTokens = committoken.NewSigner([]byte(cfg.HomeRegionCookieSecret))
670		}
671	
672		deps.refreshStore = authn.NewRefreshStore(regionalPool)
673		deps.authRequestStore = authn.NewAuthRequestStore(regionalPool)
674		deps.pluginAuthorizations = authn.NewPluginAuthorizationStore(regionalPool)
675	
676		deps.idpSessionStore = authn.NewSessionStore(regionalPool, authn.IdpSessionTable, 24*time.Hour)
677		deps.consoleSessionStore = authn.NewSessionStore(regionalPool, authn.ConsoleSessionTable, 24*time.Hour)
678		deps.deviceGrantStore = authn.NewDeviceGrantStore(regionalPool)
679	
680		isSecure := true
681		// idp_session is host-only on the auth host — it represents the
682		// user's session with the IdP and is read only by handlers on the
683		// auth origin. No Domain so the cookie doesn't leak to console.*.
684		deps.idpCookie = authn.NewSessionCookie("idp_session", isSecure, "", 24*time.Hour)
685		// console_session is host-only on the console host. The OAuth
686		// redirect_uri targets the console origin, so Set-Cookie there is
687		// host-scoped by construction — no need to span the auth↔console
688		// boundary via Domain. Sibling jurisdictions (us.console.* vs
689		// eu.console.*) get their own slot and can't clobber each other.
690		deps.consoleCookie = authn.NewSessionCookie("console_session", isSecure, "", 24*time.Hour)
691		// Browser three-tier session cookies (ADR 20260527), host-only on the
692		// auth origin alongside idp_session. Max-Age tracks each tier's TTL: the
693		// login JWT (8h) and the opaque refresh token (7d browser).
694		deps.loginCookie = authn.NewSessionCookie("login", isSecure, "", authn.LoginTokenTTL)
695		deps.refreshCookie = authn.NewSessionCookie("refresh", isSecure, "", authn.BrowserRefreshTokenTTL)
696	
697		// Regional is production-only; anything but https leaks the console
698		// client_secret on the RP→IdP back-channel and silently breaks login
699		// (cookies are minted with Secure=true above, which browsers drop on
700		// non-HTTPS connections). No localhost exemption — local dev serves
701		// HTTPS via the mkcert bundle.
702		if !strings.HasPrefix(cfg.AuthBaseURL, "https://") {
703			cleanup()
704			return deps, func() {}, fmt.Errorf("ENTIRE_CORE_AUTH_BASE_URL must be https:// in regional mode (got %q)", cfg.AuthBaseURL)
705		}
706		mtlsClients, err := regionalMTLSClients(ctx, cfg, deps.clusterStore)
707		if err != nil {
708			cleanup()
709			return deps, func() {}, err
710		}
711		clientRegistry, consoleClient, err := buildOAuthClientRegistry(ctx, cfg, mtlsClients...)
712		if err != nil {
713			cleanup()
714			return deps, func() {}, err
715		}
716		deps.clientRegistry = clientRegistry
717		deps.consoleClientID = consoleClient.ID
718		deps.consoleClientSecret = REDACTED
719	
720		// Sibling discovery uses the raw JURISDICTION_AUTH_HOSTS, never the
721		// merged-with-REGION_HOSTS map: JWT iss/aud are always AuthBaseURL,
722		// never console URL, so a console-host fallback can't legitimately
723		// appear here. errOnPartialJurisdictionAuthHosts above already
724		// refused boot if the map is partial.
725		siblingURLs := siblingAuthBaseURLs(authHostsRaw, cfg.AuthBaseURL)
726		deps.siblingAuthBaseURLs = siblingURLs
727		// The waitlist approval gate (assertAccountApproved) treats a nil
728		// IdentitySvc as "approval not wired" and fails OPEN — a deliberate
729		// unit-test seam. Production must never construct Storage without it,
730		// or the gate would silently let waitlisted accounts mint repo tokens.
731		if deps.identitySvc == nil {
732			cleanup()
733			return deps, func() {}, errors.New("oidc storage: IdentitySvc is required (waitlist approval gate fails open without it)")
734		}
735	
736		var issuerIntrospect oidcop.IssuerIntrospector
737		if len(siblingURLs) > 0 {
738			// NewStorage builds a per-sibling JWKSVerifier from siblingURLs,
739			// each pointed at that sibling's remote JWKS (COR-382). Cross-juris
740			// exchange also gates on the subject's current account state before
741			// minting a foreign-session token — see ADR 20260520. The state
742			// lives in global tables, so the check runs against the shared DB
743			// instead of dialing the home region's introspect endpoint.
744			issuerIntrospect = oidcop.NewLocalIssuerIntrospector(deps.identitySvc)
745		}
746	
747		automationLimiter := oidcop.NewAutomationExchangeLimiter(oidcop.AutomationExchangeRateConfig{
748			PerMinute: cfg.AutomationExchangeRatePerMinute,
749			Burst:     cfg.AutomationExchangeBurst,
750		})
751		pluginTokenLimiter := oidcop.NewPluginTokenLimiter(cfg.PluginTokenRatePerMinute, cfg.PluginTokenBurst)
752		oidcStorage := oidcop.NewStorage(oidcop.StorageConfig{
753			KeyStore:              deps.keyStore,
754			RefreshStore:          deps.refreshStore,
755			IdentitySvc:           deps.identitySvc,
756			ClientRegistry:        deps.clientRegistry,
757			CIMDResolver:          cimd.NewResolver(cimd.Config{}),
758			PluginCatalog:         deps.pluginCatalog,
759			AuthRequestStore:      deps.authRequestStore,
760			DeviceGrantStore:      deps.deviceGrantStore,
761			Authz:                 deps.authzSvc,
762			PlatformAdminResource: "platform:" + coreapi.PlatformResourceID,
763			RepoResolver:          deps.resourceSvc,
764			OrgLister:             deps.resourceSvc,
765			ClusterResolver:       newClusterResolver(deps.resourceSvc, deps.clusterStore, deps.mirrorRepoSvc),
766			CIWebhooksURL:         cfg.CIWebhooksURL,
767			CIWebhooksURLs:        cfg.CIWebhooksURLs,
768			MirrorResolver:        newMirrorResolver(deps.mirrorRepoSvc),
769			NativeMirrorResolver:  deps.nativeMirrorSvc,
770			OIDCFed:               deps.oidcfedSvc,
771			ServiceAccount:        deps.serviceAccountSvc,
772			Automation:            deps.automationSvc,
773			RepoGroupChecker:      deps.resourceSvc,
774			AutomationLimiter:     automationLimiter,
775			PluginTokenLimiter:    pluginTokenLimiter,
776			Audit:                 deps.domainAudit,
777			AuthCodeResources:     authn.NewAuthCodeResourceRegistry(cfg.AuthCodeResourceURLs),
778			LoginAud:              cfg.AuthBaseURL,
779			LoginTokenTTL:         deps.jwtIssuer.TTL(),
780			SiblingAuthBaseURLs:   siblingURLs,
781			IssuerIntrospector:    issuerIntrospect,
782			Analytics:             deps.analyticsClient,
783		})
784		deps.pluginTokens = oidcStorage
785		deps.oidcProvider, err = oidcop.NewProvider(cfg.AuthBaseURL, oidcStorage)
786		if err != nil {
787			cleanup()
788			return deps, func() {}, fmt.Errorf("construct oidc provider: %w", err)
789		}
790		ratelimit.StartCleanup(ctx, automationLimiter)
791		ratelimit.StartCleanup(ctx, pluginTokenLimiter)
792		// Same reasoning as keyStore.StartBackgroundRefresh above: a quiet pod's
793		// first cross-region exchange after a deploy otherwise pays the sibling
794		// JWKS fetch on the request path.
795		oidcStorage.WarmSiblingJWKS(ctx)
796	
797		deps.loginFlow = loginflow.New(loginflow.Config{
798			Identity:          deps.identitySvc,
799			Regional:          deps.regionalSvc,
800			Jurisdiction:      cfg.Jurisdiction,
801			CEOWelcomeEnabled: cfg.CEOWelcomeEnabled,
802			// Backfills first-login mirror access in the background and creates the
803			// personal mirrors project of an already installed GitHub user. Regional
804			// wires the full perms stack (SpiceDB read+write via dialSpiceDB, plus the
805			// global-pool githubPerms / mirrorRepoSvc / resourceSvc set above), so
806			// buildMirrorPermsReconciler is non-nil here and a fresh account gains its
807			// source-managed grants at first login rather than waiting for the
808			// periodic reconciler sweep. This matters more since ENT-1058: new-user
809			// account creation moved from the global picker to this regional login.
810			OnAccountCreated: chainAccountHooks(mirrorPermsAccountBackfill(&deps), mirrorsProjectAccountHook(buildMirrorsProjectProvisioner(ctx, cfg, &deps), mirrorsProjectTriggerSignup)),
811			EmailOutbox:      emailEnqueuerOrNilAuthn(deps.emailOutbox),
812		})
813	
814		deps.systemJWT = authn.NewJWTIssuer(deps.keyStore, 1*time.Hour, cfg.IssuerClaim(), cfg.IssuerClaim())
815		deps.systemLogin = authn.NewSystemLogin([]string{cfg.BreakGlassToken, cfg.BreakGlassTokenOld})
816	
817		// WorkOS persistence lives in the global pool (org WorkOS IDs,
818		// event ledger, event cursor, account state flag).
819		wosSvc, err := buildWorkOSService(ctx, cfg, globalPool, deps.identitySvc, deps.resourceSvc)
820		if err != nil {
821			cleanup()
822			return deps, func() {}, err
823		}
824		deps.workosSvc = wosSvc
825	
826		// No migrations — init containers handle that.
827	
828		return deps, cleanup, nil
829	}

# Row-level locality for region-affine tables in the global CockroachDB

Status: Accepted

## TLDR

`ALTER DATABASE entirecore` is now multi-region on the `global-v2` cluster and
two locality mechanisms are already in use: `GLOBAL` for read-everywhere lookup
tables (`clusters`, `repo_registry`/`repo_facts`/`repo_group` — migrations
`resource/026` and `resource/033`) and per-query follower reads for
staleness-tolerant reads (ADR
[20260529-entire-core-crdb-read-locality](20260529-entire-core-crdb-read-locality.md)).
Neither helps a **claim queue**: a `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` poll can never be a
follower read, and `GLOBAL` would tax every enqueue with commit-wait while
leaving the leaseholder in one region anyway.

This ADR adopts the third mechanism, **`REGIONAL BY ROW`** ("RBR"), for tables
whose rows already belong to exactly one jurisdiction, and fixes **how** rows
get homed: **implicitly, by the writing SQL gateway's region**, never by an
explicit region column or a per-environment region mapping.

Pass 1 (this change, four tables):

| table | migration | locality | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `identity.erasure_tombstones` | `identity/029` | `GLOBAL` | fresh (non-AOST) read per push author in every region; near-never written |
| `identity.email_outbox` | `identity/030` | `REGIONAL BY ROW` | per-jurisdiction claim queue, 1s poll, `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` |
| `oidcfed.workload_identity_providers` | `oidcfed/004` | `GLOBAL` | near-static manifest registry, read by `issuer_url` on the STS path from every region |
| `nativemirror.native_mirror_deletion_outbox` | `nativemirror/004` | `REGIONAL BY ROW` | per-jurisdiction claim queue, 15s poll, written by the same jurisdiction's executor |

No application code changes. Locality DDL only.

## Context

The `entirecore` database on `global-v2` is multi-region with the primary region
in the US. A table created without a locality clause is
`REGIONAL BY TABLE IN PRIMARY REGION`, so its leaseholder is in the US and every
present-time read or write from EU/AU/IN pays one cross-region round trip
(measured: EU→US ~105ms, AU→US ~385ms p50 / ~948ms p95 — see
20260529 and `resource/033`).

Three mechanisms remove that hop; each fits a different access shape:

| | follower read | `GLOBAL` | `REGIONAL BY ROW` |
|---|---|---|---|
| out-of-region read | local | local | local **for rows homed here** |
| freshness | ~4.8s stale | fresh | fresh |
| write cost | unchanged | commit-wait everywhere | unchanged (local leaseholder) |
| locking reads (`FOR UPDATE`) | **not possible** | leaseholder still remote | **local** |
| where it lives | per query | per-table DDL | per-table DDL + a hidden row column |

The gap this ADR fills is the bottom-left cell. We run several
**per-jurisdiction claim queues** — transactional outboxes drained by the region
that owns the rows:

- `email_outbox`: each region's relay polls every 1s with
  `WHERE home_jurisdiction = $1 ORDER BY id LIMIT $n FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`,
  publishes, then deletes the acked ids (`core/email/outbox.go:130-133`, `:196`).
- `native_mirror_deletion_outbox`: each jurisdiction's executor polls every 15s
  with `WHERE jurisdiction = $1 ORDER BY created_at, repo_id LIMIT $n` and
  deletes each row after its `PubAck` (`core/repodeletion/outbox.go:146-152`).
  The row is enqueued in the same transaction as the authoritative
  `native_mirrors` DELETE (`core/nativemirror/nativemirror.go:668-679`).

Both are pure region-affine workloads: the rows a region writes are exactly the
rows it later claims. Yet both live on a table whose leaseholder is in the US, so
every tick of every non-US relay crosses an ocean to read and then again to
delete rows nobody else will ever touch.

Two read-everywhere tables round out the pass. They are not queues; they are the
same profile as `clusters` (migration 026), missed at the time:

- `erasure_tombstones` — `IsTombstoned` (`core/erasureledger/ledger.go:479-487`)
  is a deliberately **fresh** read; a stale miss resurrects PII the erasure
  removed. It runs per push author in every region's verified-email consumer
  (`internal/entirecore/verifiedemailwebhook/apply.go:135-144`, the fail-closed
  guard before the `verified_emails` upsert). Writes happen only when an erasure
  completes.
- `workload_identity_providers` — manifest-reconciled registry
  (`core/oidcfed/store.go:61-71`), read by `issuer_url` twice per federated
  token exchange from every region. It was read via follower-read-with-fresh-
  fallback precisely because the fresh read was cross-region; the `GLOBAL`
  conversion removes that reason, so this change also **deletes** that dance in
  favour of a single fresh read (`core/oidcfed/store.go` `GetProviderByIssuer`).
  That is the one place in this pass where a locality change lets us delete code
  rather than just move latency.

## Decision

### 1. Adopt `REGIONAL BY ROW` for region-affine tables

Convert a table to RBR when a row's jurisdiction is fixed at write time and the
same jurisdiction is the one that later reads, locks, updates or deletes it.
Claim queues qualify; read-everywhere lookup tables do not (those get `GLOBAL`).

### 2. Home rows implicitly, via the gateway region

RBR adds a hidden `crdb_region` column defaulting to
`default_to_database_primary_region(gateway_region())`. Our SQL gateways are
region-local (a `BEGIN` from the EU core against the global cluster is ~1.7ms —
the DSN geo-routes to a Frankfurt gateway, see 20260529), so **a row is homed in
the region of the core that wrote it**, with no application involvement.

We deliberately do **not**:

- add an explicit `crdb_region` column to the table definition,
- write a `CASE jurisdiction WHEN 'eu' THEN 'aws-eu-central-1' ...` mapping,
- add `crdb_region` predicates to queries.

The reason is hard: **region names may never appear in a migration.** The
prod/staging database region enums are `aws-`-prefixed (`aws-us-east-2`, …),
dev/CI is bare (`us-east-2`), and staging's primary is a different region again.
A shared goose migration that names regions would either fail or, worse, apply
different semantics per environment. Pure `SET LOCALITY` statements are the only
form that is environment-agnostic, and implicit homing is the only homing that
needs no region literal.

The cost of implicit homing is that homing follows the **writer's** region rather
than the row's `jurisdiction`/`home_jurisdiction` column. For both pass-1 queues
those coincide today. If they ever diverge, the row is still claimed and
delivered correctly — the claim filters on the jurisdiction column, not on
`crdb_region` — it just sits in a remote partition and that claim stops being
local. **Corollary footgun, recorded in both migrations:** do not "optimize" a
claim query by adding a `crdb_region` predicate. That would convert a
mis-homed row from *slow* into *stranded forever*.

### 3. Pass 1 scope

`erasure_tombstones` and `workload_identity_providers` → `GLOBAL`.
`email_outbox` and `native_mirror_deletion_outbox` → `REGIONAL BY ROW`.

Beyond the primary key, none of the four carries a unique constraint or a foreign
key (`identity/018`, `identity/020`, `identity/025`, `nativemirror/003`,
`oidcfed/001`) — which is what makes them the cheapest possible first pass (see
Trade-offs).

### 4. Planned pass 2

Candidates whose rows are account- or placement-affine, deferred to a second
pass because each has a unique constraint, a foreign key, or a
read-from-everywhere caller that needs its own analysis first:

| table | affinity | complication |
|---|---|---|
| `github_user_tokens` | account home jurisdiction | `account_id` PK only, no FK — likely the easiest pass-2 win |
| `mirror_repos` | `cluster_slug` | extra `UNIQUE (github_repo_id, cluster_slug)` + FK to `github_repos` |
| `github_mirror_repo_urls` | `cluster_slug` (PK prefix) | FK to `mirror_repos`; would want the parent converted first |
| `mirror_author_backfills` | placement's cluster | claim/lease table; needs the same poll analysis as pass 1 |
| `native_replicas` | `cluster_slug` | FK to `repo_group` (deliberately non-cascading, load-bearing for teardown) |

### 5. Explicitly deferred, with reasons

- **`github_*` perms read-models** (`github_user_repo_access`, `github_users`,
  `github_repos`, `github_installations`). No per-row region affinity: a repo's
  edges are written by whichever cell ingested the webhook and read by every
  cell's reconciler. The user-facing list/readiness reads are already follower
  reads with fresh fallback (`core/githubperms/store.go:650`, `:669`, `:827`,
  `:958`), so the remaining fresh reads are the sync/reconcile paths. On top of
  that, `github_user_repo_access` FKs both `github_users` and `github_repos`.
  This reaffirms 20260529's deferral of RBR here.
- **`repo_registry`, `repo_group`, `repo_facts`** stay `GLOBAL` (migration 033).
  They are read by *cross-jurisdiction* index scans (the global sorted repo
  list), which is the shape RBR is worst at.
- **`account_erasure_outbox`** is anti-affine: every jurisdiction polls every
  row it has not yet completed
  (`WHERE NOT ($1 = ANY(done_jurisdictions))`, `core/accounterasure/outbox.go:224`,
  and the `array_append` update at `:314`). Under RBR each region's poll would
  fan out across all partitions on every tick and its update would usually be a
  remote write. RBR would make this worse, not better; `GLOBAL` is the mechanism
  to evaluate here if it ever becomes hot.
- **`orgs`, `projects`** — the hot reads are already follower reads
  (`core/resource/store.go`), and the admin/list paths scan across
  jurisdictions, so RBR would fan those out for no read win.
  *Amended 2026-10-16:* `projects` is `GLOBAL` (coreglobal 015). The
  `/repos?filter=` name resolution (`GetProjectByName`) is a fresh read and
  was the last cross-region hop on the BFF repo-lookup path, ~380ms from
  Australia. The table is written only at project create and delete.
- **`github_email_identities`** — written from multiple regions (webhook feed
  plus mirror backfill) with no region key on the row, and its hot read is
  already a follower read with fresh fallback
  (`core/identity/github_email_identities.go:151-152`).

## Trade-offs

- **Point lookups by bare primary key from a non-home region get slower in the
  worst case.** RBR implicitly prefixes every index with `crdb_region`, so a
  lookup that does not constrain the region becomes a locality-optimized
